definition_zh: 铜绿；包浆；岁月留下的痕迹；韵味
definition_en: a thin coloured layer that time, use, or air leaves on a surface, or the charm it gives
core_image: 老铜锁表面那层暗绿的光泽，被手摸得温润发亮
scene: 老宅的木门上挂着一把铜锁，锁身早已蒙上暗绿的锈色，像一层温润的外壳。Years of handling had given the brass handle a soft green patina.
sceneCN: 这里 patina 是「铜绿」（第 1 个义项：金属表面因氧化形成的有色薄层）；句意是：多年把玩让那黄铜把手覆上了一层柔和的绿锈。画面里有木门、铜锁和被手掌磨亮的一圈痕迹。

pos.zh: 铜绿；包浆；岁月痕迹；韵味

derivatives.zh: patina 加后缀 -ed 构成的形容词，义为「覆有包浆的；经过做旧处理的」
patina 加后缀 -ation 构成的名词，义为「生成包浆的过程」
patina 加后缀 -ize 构成的动词，义为「使（金属）生锈变色」

senses.title: A green film on metal
senses.definition: a thin green or brownish layer that forms on copper and bronze when they are exposed to air
senses.definitionCN: 铜与青铜暴露在空气中后在其表面形成的绿色或褐色薄层
senses.example: The statue has a green patina from years of rain.
senses.exampleCN: 这座雕像因多年雨淋而覆上一层铜绿。
senses.why: The word comes from Latin patina, a shallow dish, and early writers saw a green crust as something laid thinly over metal like a coating in a pan.
senses.whyCN: patina 来自拉丁语 patina，原指浅盘；早期用法把金属上那层薄薄的绿壳看作像盘中薄薄铺开的一层，于是「薄膜」的画面落在了铜器表面，这就是最具体的铜绿义。

senses.title: A sheen from long use
senses.definition: the soft shine that repeated handling and time give to a surface
senses.definitionCN: 长期把玩与时间在表面上留下的柔和光泽
senses.example: The table has a warm patina where hands have rested.
senses.exampleCN: 桌面被双手摩挲的地方泛着一层温润的包浆。
senses.why: If a surface can acquire a layer by itself, it can also acquire a layer from touch, so the film becomes evidence of wear rather than of air.
senses.whyCN: 既然表面能靠空气自行长出一层，也就能靠手反复触摸长出一层；于是那层「膜」从化学反应的产物，变成了有人使用过的证据，词义随之温柔起来。

senses.title: A trace of age
senses.definition: a visible sign that something is old and has lasted a long time
senses.definitionCN: 表明某物年岁已久、历经时间的可见痕迹
senses.example: The building wears a patina of age on every wall.
senses.exampleCN: 这座建筑的每面墙都带着岁月的痕迹。
senses.why: Once the film means use, it also means time, and the word can name the whole look of age that vintage things carry.
senses.whyCN: 当那层膜意味着「被用过」，它同时也就意味着「过了很久」；于是这个词可以整体指一件旧物身上那种由时间累积出来的质感，而不只是某一层物质。

senses.title: A surface of respectability
senses.definition: an attractive outer layer or appearance that hides something you may not want to see
senses.definitionCN: 讨人喜欢的外层或外表，往往遮住人们不太想看到的东西
senses.example: The firm has a patina of respectability it does not deserve.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司披着一层它并不配有的体面外衣。
senses.why: The image of a thin attractive layer is easily used for appearance, and when that appearance only covers something else, the word gains an ironic edge.
senses.whyCN: 「薄而好看的一层」这个画面天然适合用来比喻门面；当这层好看只负责遮盖下面的东西时，patina 就带上了讽刺意味，暗示外表与实际并不一致。

senses.title: Mellow charm
senses.definition: the pleasant quality that ageing or experience gives to a thing, sound, or style
senses.definitionCN: 老化或阅历赋予事物、声音或风格的宜人特质
senses.example: His voice has the patina of decades on the road.
senses.exampleCN: 他的嗓音带着几十年奔波打磨出的韵味。
senses.why: Once age is seen as an addition rather than a loss, the trace becomes a quality, and the word can describe a charm that could not be made at once.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把「老化」看成加了一层，而不是掉了一层，痕迹就变成了优点；patina 于是能形容一种无法速成、只能慢慢养出来的韵味。

senses.title: A deliberately applied finish
senses.definition: an artificial finish added to a new object so that it looks old
senses.definitionCN: 为让新物件显得陈旧而人为添加的涂层
senses.example: The decorators applied a dark patina to the new cabinet.
senses.exampleCN: 装修工人给新柜子刷上了一层深色做旧涂层。
senses.why: Time can be imitated, so the visible layer can be manufactured, and the word comes to name a technique in art and design rather than a natural process.
senses.whyCN: 时间可以被模仿，所以那层可见的膜也能被人工制造出来；patina 由此从自然过程变成了一门手艺的名字，设计师用它来说明「新做旧」的效果。

intro.en: Patina comes from Latin patina, a shallow dish, and its sense of a surface film grew in French and Italian art writing before English borrowed it.
intro.cn: patina 来自拉丁语 patina（浅盘）；「表面薄膜」这一义项是在法语与意大利语的艺术用语中发展出来、再被英语借走的。

items.en: Patina names a shallow pan or dish used for cooking and serving.
items.cn: 拉丁语 patina 指烹调和盛放食物用的浅盘。

items.en: Some Latin writers borrow the Greek term for such a dish.
items.cn: 部分拉丁作家把这层意思与希腊语的同名器物词相联系。

items.en: Art writers use patina for the green surface of old bronze.
items.cn: 艺术评论家用这个词指旧青铜表面的绿锈。

items.en: English takes patina from Italian and French for the film on metal.
items.cn: 英语从意大利语与法语借入，指金属表面的一层薄膜。

items.en: Writers extend the word to furniture, voices, and even reputations.
items.cn: 作家把它扩展到家具、嗓音乃至名声之上。

note.en: Patina sits beside patinated and patination in form, and beside sheen and glow in meaning.
note.cn: patina 在形式上与 patinated、patination 相邻，在意义上与 sheen、glow 等词相邻。

entries.definition: covered with a surface film from age or treatment
the process of forming a patina
the kneecap
entries.definitionCN: 膝盖骨（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a soft shine on a surface
the brightness of a surface that reflects light
the green substance formed on copper by air

normalIntro.en: Patina is the thin layer that time leaves on a surface, first of metal and then of almost anything.
normalIntro.cn: patina 是时间在表面上留下的薄薄一层，先是金属，后来几乎可以是任何东西。

normal.en: A green patina is the oxide layer on copper and bronze.
normal.cn: green patina 就是铜与青铜上的氧化层。

normal.en: The verb patinate means to give something such a surface.
normal.cn: 动词 patinate 意思是使某物带上这种表面。

normal.en: Patination names the process, while patina names the result.
normal.cn: patination 指过程，patina 指结果。

normal.en: The phrase a patina of age describes the look of time on an object.
normal.cn: 短语「a patina of age」描述时间在物件上留下的样子。

normal.en: Beware of patella, which is about the knee and shares nothing but a spelling.
normal.cn: 注意 patella 指膝盖骨，除拼写外毫无关系。

abstract.en: Picture a green coin in a museum case, its surface soft and even.
abstract.cn: 想象展柜里一枚泛绿的老硬币，表面匀净柔和。

abstract.en: Feel a stair rail polished into a warm, glossy band.
abstract.cn: 想象一根被摸得温热发亮的楼梯扶手。

abstract.en: Think of a torn leather chair worn smooth where people always sat.
abstract.cn: 想象一把旧皮椅，人常坐的地方被磨得光滑。

examples.en: Rain had left a green patina on the church bells.
examples.cn: 雨水在教堂的铜钟上留下一层铜绿。

examples.en: Antique shops sell new lamps with a fake patina.
examples.cn: 古玩店售卖带人造做旧涂层的新灯。

examples.en: The old flagstone floor has a patina that no new floor can copy.
examples.cn: 旧石板地面上的那层包浆，新铺的地面怎么也复制不来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕替娜」——怕被时间替换掉，所以先给自己镀上一层绿壳：一层薄薄的铜绿。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 patina（浅盘、平底锅）→ 意大利语与法语艺术用语中的 patina（青铜绿锈）→ 英语 patina。拉丁语词形本身来源不确定，一般认为与希腊语同名器物词 patane 有关，但存在争议；核心义由「平铺的薄盘」引申为「覆在表面的一层薄膜」。

sensesIntro.en: Patina begins as a thin film on metal, widens to the shine of use and the look of age, and ends as a surface that can be praised or faked.
sensesIntro.cn: patina 从金属表面的薄膜出发，扩展到使用留下的光泽与年岁带来的痕迹，最终成为可以被赞美、也可以被伪造的一层表面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin green film lying evenly on an old bronze handle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层薄薄的绿膜均匀覆在旧铜把手上。

branches.en: The chemical film on copper is the oldest concrete sense.
branches.cn: 铜表面的化学薄膜是最早的具体义项。

branches.en: Use and age turn the film into a mark of time.
branches.cn: 使用与年岁把薄膜变成时间的记号。

branches.en: The same thin layer becomes a surface that hides.
branches.cn: 同一层薄膜也可变成遮掩事物的门面。

branches.en: Age as charm is the praised end, and the fake finish is the made end.
branches.cn: 韵味的尽头是被赞美的一层，做旧涂层则是被人工制造的一层。

branches.en: Both the green film and the mellow charm are things only time can give.
branches.cn: 绿锈与韵味都是只有时间才给得出来的东西。

intro.en: Patina is a borrowed Latin noun with no productive English affix, but English has grown three members of its family around it.
intro.cn: patina 是借入的拉丁语名词，本身不含能产的英语词缀，但英语已围绕它长出三个同族词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is the noun patina, a shallow dish; the modern sense arrived through Italian and French art writing.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁语来源是名词 patina（浅盘），现代义项是经由意大利语与法语的艺术用语传入的。

items.example: Patina first named a flat dish used at table.
items.exampleCN: patina 最初指餐桌上用的平底浅盘。

items.example: The English noun keeps the flat film picture.
items.exampleCN: 英语名词保留了「平铺薄膜」的画面。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms patinated.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 patinated。

items.example: Patinated describes bronze that has aged.
items.exampleCN: patinated 形容已经老化的青铜。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms patination.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 patination。

items.example: Patination is the action behind the result.
items.exampleCN: patination 是结果背后的动作。

items.example: The suffix -ize forms patinize.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 构成 patinize。

items.example: Patinize means to treat a surface.
items.exampleCN: patinize 指对表面进行处理。

items.example: Verdigris names the chemistry, not the look.
items.exampleCN: verdigris 说的是化学物质，而非外观感受。

definition_zh: 家长；族长；主教；元老；创始人
definition_en: the senior male head of a family, clan, or group, especially one whose authority is accepted because of age
core_image: 一位白须老者坐在院落正中，儿孙围着他绕成一圈
scene: 院子里的石凳上坐着一位白发老者，膝边围着儿孙，全家人的婚丧嫁娶都要先问他的主意。In a village of herders, the patriarch still decides how the families divide the grazing land.
sceneCN: 这里 patriarch 是「族长、家长」（第 1 个义项：以年长与父系血缘为使、对家族拥有权威的男性长辈）；句意是：在一个牧民村落里，族长仍然决定各家如何分配牧场。画面中出现的是石凳、拐杖和围坐的家人。

pos.zh: 家长；族长；主教；元老；创始人

derivatives.zh: patriarch 加后缀 -y 构成的名词，义为「父权制；由男性长者主导的社会结构」
patriarch 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「父权的；家长制的」
patriarch 加后缀 -ate 构成的名词，义为「宗主教的职位、任期或辖区」

senses.title: The male head of a family
senses.definition: the oldest or most senior man in a family or clan, whose decisions are respected
senses.definitionCN: 家族或氏族中最年长或地位最尊的男性，其决定受到尊重
senses.example: The patriarch divided the land among his four sons.
senses.exampleCN: 族长把土地分给了四个儿子。
senses.why: The first part comes from Greek pater, father, and the second from arkhe, rule, so a patriarch is built as a father who rules.
senses.whyCN: 前半来自希腊语 pater（父亲），后半来自 arkhe（统治、起始），所以 patriarch 的构词意思就是「以父亲身份行使统领的人」；最直接的落点，就是把一家之主的权威写进词里。

senses.title: A founding ancestor
senses.definition: an early ancestor from whom a whole people or lineage traces its descent
senses.definitionCN: 被整个民族或家族追溯为源头的远古祖先
senses.example: The book opens with the patriarch of the clan crossing the river.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书从那位渡河的氏祖先人写起。
senses.why: If the head rules, the first head founds, and the word naturally travels back in time to the ancestor at the beginning of the line.
senses.whyCN: 既然族长在当下掌权，那么最早的那个「掌权者」就自然成为开创者；词义于是顺着血缘往回推，落到整条家族线起点上的那位祖先。

senses.title: A father figure in the Bible
senses.definition: one of the early fathers of the Jewish and Christian traditions, such as Abraham
senses.definitionCN: 犹太教与基督教传统中最早的先祖，如亚伯拉罕
senses.example: Abraham is honoured as a patriarch of two faiths.
senses.exampleCN: 亚伯拉罕被尊为两种信仰共同的族长。
senses.why: Religious use fixes the word to the founding fathers of a tradition, where father and founder are the same person.
senses.whyCN: 宗教文本把「父」与「源」合成一体：一个传统最早的父辈，也正是这个传统的源头，所以这个词在经文里专指那些被追溯的先祖。

senses.title: A senior bishop
senses.definition: a title for certain bishops in the eastern churches and in Rome
senses.definitionCN: 东方教会与罗马教会中对某些主教的尊称
senses.example: The patriarch of Jerusalem led the procession.
senses.exampleCN: 耶路撒冷宗主教主持了这场游行。
senses.why: Church government borrowed the family picture and made the senior cleric of a region the father of the faithful.
senses.whyCN: 教会借用了家庭画面，把某一地区的最高神职人员称为信众的「父亲」；于是对宗教团体的统领权，被同一个词从家族搬到了教会。

senses.title: A respected elder
senses.definition: an older man whose long experience makes others look to him for guidance
senses.definitionCN: 因阅历深厚而被他人视为靠山与向导的年长男性
senses.example: He is the patriarch of the department and trains every new teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 他是系里的元老，每有新教师都由他来带。
senses.why: Strip away kinship and religion and what remains is age plus authority, which any group can grant to its oldest member.
senses.whyCN: 把血缘与宗教抽掉，剩下的正是「年长加上权威」；任何团体都可以把这一组合交给自己最老的那位成员，所以这个词能指一个行业或机构里的前辈。

senses.title: The founder of a movement
senses.definition: the first leader who began an institution, movement, or school of thought
senses.definitionCN: 开创某个机构、运动或学派的第一位领导者
senses.example: The patriarch of modern geology began as a working surveyor.
senses.exampleCN: 这位现代地质学的奠基人最初只是一名测量员。
senses.why: The founder is a father in time rather than in blood, and the word follows the same step from head to beginning.
senses.whyCN: 创始人是时间意义上的父亲，而不是血缘上的父亲；patriarch 沿着「从当下掌权追溯到最初起源」的同一条路，把父亲的形象借给了一个学科或运动的开端。

intro.en: Patriarch comes from Greek patriarkhes, formed from pater, father, and arkhein, to rule, and reached English through Latin and Old French by the twelfth century.
intro.cn: patriarch 源自希腊语 patriarkhes，由 pater（父亲）与 arkhein（统治）构成，经拉丁语与古法语进入英语，最早见于十二世纪。

items.en: Pater means father, and arkhes means leader or ruler.
items.cn: pater 意为父亲，arkhes 意为首领或统治者。

items.en: Patriarkhes names the father of a tribe and, later, a chief bishop.
items.cn: patriarkhes 指一族之父，后来也指首席主教。

items.en: Patriarcha appears in church Latin for senior bishops.
items.cn: patriarcha 在教会拉丁语中指高阶主教。

items.en: Patriarche carries the word into French usage.
items.cn: patriarche 把该词带入法语用法。

items.en: Patriarch arrives in English first as an ecclesiastical title.
items.cn: 英语中 patriarch 最初用作教会头衔。

items.en: The sense widens to the head of any family, group, or movement.
items.cn: 后来范围扩展到任何家庭、团体或运动的领头人。

note.en: Patriarch sits beside the same Greek family in form, and beside words for elders and leaders in meaning.
note.cn: 从形式上看 patriarch 与同一希腊词族的词相邻，从意义上看与表示长辈与领袖的词相邻。

entries.definition: ruled or dominated by men
a system in which men hold the main power
a person who supports or protects someone
entries.definitionCN: 赞助人；庇护人（与 pater 同源）

entries.definition: an older person with authority in a group
the leader of a tribe or clan
a woman who heads a family or group
entries.definitionCN: 女家长；女族长（母亲一侧的对应词）

normalIntro.en: Patriarch is two Greek pieces joined: pater for father, arkhe for rule, so the ruler sits inside the father.
normalIntro.cn: patriarch 由两块希腊语拼成：pater 是父亲，arkhe 是统治，所以「统治者」就住在「父亲」里面。

normal.en: Patr- means father, as in paternal and paternity.
normal.cn: patr- 表示父亲，如 paternal 与 paternity。

normal.en: The second part of patriarch, -arch, means ruler, as in monarch and anarchy.
normal.cn: patriarch 的后半 -arch 表示统治者，如 monarch 与 anarchy。

normal.en: Adding -y makes patriarchy, a system rather than one man.
normal.cn: 加 -y 得到 patriarchy，指制度而不是一个人。

normal.en: Adding -al makes patriarchal, the adjective for that system.
normal.cn: 加 -al 得到形容词 patriarchal，用来描述这种制度。

normal.en: The matching word with mother at the front is matriarch.
normal.cn: 把开头换成母亲的对应词是 matriarch。

abstract.en: Picture an old man on a stone chair, his stick planted between his feet.
abstract.cn: 想象石凳上的一位老人，拐杖立在两膝之间。

abstract.en: Imagine a family photograph in which all the faces lean toward one grey head.
abstract.cn: 想象一张全家福，所有面孔都朝着一颗灰白的头。

abstract.en: Think of a sealed book at the front of a long shelf of books.
abstract.cn: 想象长书架最前端摆着一本封好的书。

examples.en: The patriarch of the family still keeps the keys to every house.
examples.cn: 这个家族的家长仍保管着每座房子的钥匙。

examples.en: In many villages the oldest men act as patriarchs and settle disputes.
examples.cn: 在许多村庄里，最年长的男子担任族老并调解纠纷。

examples.en: Critics call this a patriarchal system, although the adjective is more common.
examples.cn: 批评者称这是一个父权制度，尽管形容词形式更常用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派特里克」——派出去特别厉害的那一位克星：家里一出事，众人就派他去拿主意，于是他就是族长。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 pater（父亲）+ arkhein（统治，源自名词 arkhe「起始、统治」）→ 希腊语 patriarkhes → 拉丁语 patriarcha → 古法语 patriarche → 英语 patriarch。同一词根还生出 patron、patriot、pattern；arch- 表示「首要、统领」的用法见于 archbishop。

sensesIntro.en: Patriarch begins with the father who rules a household, moves back in time to the founding ancestor, and then widens to any senior figure or founder.
sensesIntro.cn: patriarch 从掌权的父亲出发，顺着时间回溯到开创家族的始祖，再扩展到任何地位尊崇的长辈或奠基者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white-haired old man at the centre, everyone else facing him.
core.cn: 核心意象：白须老者坐在中央，其余人都面向他。

branches.en: The father who rules a family is the plain sense of the Greek compound.
branches.cn: 掌权的父亲是这层希腊语构词最朴素的义项。

branches.en: Tracing the line back puts the first father at the beginning of a people.
branches.cn: 把家族线回溯到起点，就得到一个民族的始祖。

branches.en: The church takes the family picture and uses it for bishops.
branches.cn: 教会借用家庭画面，把它用于主教。

branches.en: Age without blood and beginning without family give the two modern senses.
branches.cn: 去掉血缘的长辈和去掉家族的创始者，构成了两个现代义项。

branches.en: Both the father and the elder rule by being looked up to.
branches.cn: 父亲与长辈都靠被仰望而获得权威。

intro.en: Patriarch is built from the Greek combining element patri-, father, and -arch, ruler, and its family is large: patriarchate, patriarchy, patriarchal, and patron.
intro.cn: patriarch 由希腊语成分 patri-（父亲）与 -arch（统治者）构成；同族词很多，如 patriarchate、patriarchy、patriarchal 与 patron。

latinIntro.en: The Greek roots pater and arkhe reach English through Latin patriarcha and the related Latin word patronus.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊词根 pater 与 arkhe 经拉丁语 patriarcha 以及相关名词 patronus 传入英语。

items.example: Pater is the first piece of the word.
items.exampleCN: pater 是该词的第一部分。

items.example: Arkhe gives the idea of rule.
items.exampleCN: arkhe 提供「统治」这一含义。

items.example: Patri- also begins patrician and patriotism.
items.exampleCN: patri- 也用于 patrician 与 patriotism 的开头。

items.example: The element -arch appears in monarch.
items.exampleCN: 成分 -arch 出现在 monarch 中。

items.example: The prefix arch- builds archbishop.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 arch- 构成 archbishop。

items.meaning: the office or territory of a patriarch
items.example: The suffix -ate marks an office.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ate 表示某种职位。

items.example: The suffix -y forms patriarchy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成 patriarchy。

items.example: The suffix -al forms patriarchal.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 构成 patriarchal。

items.example: Anarchy shares the -arch root but has no father.
items.exampleCN: anarchy 与 -arch 同源，但没有「父亲」。

items.example: Monarch is literally a single ruler.
items.exampleCN: monarch 字面上就是单一统治者。

latinEntries.meaning: a chief bishop, a father of a people

definition_zh: 爱国的；有爱国心的
definition_en: showing love for and loyalty to your own country
core_image: 一个人把国旗紧紧抱在胸前，望向东方的晨光
scene: 国庆游行那天，老人把一面小国旗别在外套上。On the national holiday, the old man wore a small flag on his coat in a patriotic gesture.
sceneCN: 这里 patriotic 是「爱国的」（第 1 个义项：对国家怀有情感并表现出来的）；句意：国庆那天，老人把小国旗别在外套上，是一种爱国姿态。

derivatives.zh: 爱国者；源自希腊语 patriotes（同乡人）
爱国主义；由 patriot 加名词后缀 -ism 构成
以爱国的方式；由 patriotic 加 -ally 构成
不爱国的；由否定前缀 un- 加 patriotic 构成
父权制；同用 patri- 词根，但语义已转向「父权」

senses.title: Loving your own country
senses.definition: showing strong love for your own country and a desire to defend it
senses.definitionCN: 对自己的国家表现出强烈的爱并愿意维护它
senses.example: Her patriotic speech moved the whole audience.
senses.exampleCN: 她那篇爱国演讲打动了全场听众。
senses.why: The image of a person hugging the flag is the plain emotional sense, carried by the root for father and fatherland.
senses.whyCN: 抱紧国旗的画面就是最直接的情感义项，由「父亲、祖国」这一词根承载。

senses.title: Expressing national loyalty in public
senses.definition: expressed through public acts such as flags, songs, and ceremonies that declare loyalty to the nation
senses.definitionCN: 通过旗帜、歌曲、仪式等公开行为表达对国家的忠诚
senses.example: The town is famous for its patriotic parades every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小镇以每年春天的爱国游行著称。
senses.why: From a private feeling the word extends to visible customs that show the same loyalty to others.
senses.whyCN: 从私人的情感延伸为他人可见的习俗，正是同一份忠诚的外化。

senses.title: Producing works that praise the nation
senses.titleCN: 颂扬祖国的；带有爱国色彩的
senses.definition: describing works of art, music, or literature that praise the country and its history
senses.definitionCN: 形容赞颂本国及其历史的艺术、音乐或文学作品
senses.example: That composer wrote one of the best known patriotic anthems.
senses.exampleCN: 那位作曲家写了一首最著名的爱国颂歌。
senses.why: The adjective can describe the work rather than the person, since a song can carry the national feeling too.
senses.whyCN: 形容词也可以修饰作品而非个人，因为歌曲同样能承载家国情感。

senses.title: As a label for nationalism
senses.titleCN: 民族主义的；带 nationalism 色彩的批评用法
senses.definition: used with a critical tone for a show of national pride that seems excessive or aggressive
senses.definitionCN: 带批评语气，指显得过度或带有攻击性的民族自豪展示
senses.example: Critics saw the rally as a patriotic display that went too far.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者认为那场集会是一种走得太远的民族主义展示。
senses.why: When love of country is measured by hostility to others, the adjective slides toward a critical label.
senses.whyCN: 当爱国以对他人的敌意来衡量时，这个词便滑向批评性的标签。

intro.en: Patriotic comes from Greek patriotes through Latin and French, built on pater, the word for father.
intro.cn: patriotic 经拉丁语和法语传自希腊语 patriotes，词根是表示「父亲」的 pater。

items.en: Pater is the Greek word for father, and patris means fatherland.
items.cn: pater 是希腊语的「父亲」，patris 意为「父邦」。

items.en: Patriotes means fellow countryman, someone from the same fatherland.
items.cn: patriotes 意为同乡，即来自同一方父邦的人。

items.en: Patrioticus appears in medieval Latin for relating to the fatherland.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 patrioticus 表示与父邦有关的。

items.en: Patriotique spreads through French political writing.
items.cn: patriotique 经法语政治文章广泛传播。

items.en: Patriotic enters English as an adjective of love for country.
items.cn: patriotic 在十七世纪进入英语，指对国家的热爱。

items.en: The word now also marks critical or excessive forms of national pride.
items.cn: 现代英语中它还指带批评意味的、过度的民族自豪。

note.en: Patriotic sits beside its Latin family and next to the field of loyal and national words.
note.cn: patriotic 与它的拉丁词族相邻，也处在「忠诚、国家」这一意义场中。

entries.definition: a person who loves and defends his country
entries.definitionCN: 爱国者；源自希腊语同乡人

entries.definition: strong love for one own country
entries.definitionCN: 爱国主义；由 patriot 加 -ism

entries.definition: the male head of a family, or an old leader
entries.definitionCN: 家长；元老；同用 pater 词根

entries.definition: showing strong and sometimes aggressive pride in the nation
firm in support of a person, group, or country
having a deep attachment to someone or something

normalIntro.en: Patriotic carries the feeling of a fatherland, so picture the home of your family as the home of your nation.
normalIntro.cn: patriotic 蕴含「父邦」之感，可把家庭所在之处想成国家的所在。

normal.en: Patri- points to pater, father, and -otic is the adjective ending.
normal.cn: patri- 对应 pater（父亲），-otic 是形容词词尾。

normal.en: The noun patriot means a person who loves his country.
normal.cn: 名词 patriot 指热爱自己国家的人。

normal.en: Patriotism is the noun of the feeling, and patriotically is the adverb.
normal.cn: patriotism 是情感名词，patriotically 是副词。

normal.en: Fiercely patriotic often shows a tone of criticism in news writing.
normal.cn: fiercely patriotic 在新闻中常带批评语气。

normal.en: Compare patriotic with nationalistic, which is stronger and often negative.
normal.cn: 对比 nationalistic：后者的语气更强，常带贬义。

abstract.en: Picture a child standing still as the national flag rises in the morning.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子清晨立正，望着国旗升起。

abstract.en: Imagine hands pressed together, holding an old family photograph of the hometown.
abstract.cn: 想象双手合十，捧着一张家乡的全家福。

abstract.en: Think of a song played before a match, and every voice rising together.
abstract.cn: 想象比赛前奏响的歌曲，所有声音一起高扬。

examples.en: He wrote a patriotic poem about his grandfather in the war.
examples.cn: 他写了一首关于祖父参战的爱国诗。

examples.en: The crowd sang patriotic songs after the team won the final.
examples.cn: 球队赢得决赛后，人群唱起了爱国歌曲。

examples.en: Some argue that a patriotic policy should also help ordinary families.
examples.cn: 有人认为爱国的政策也应当帮助普通家庭。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派」+「吹」+「踢」——把国旗挂在胸口、爱到想「踢」正步；这只是拆音联想，与词源（pater 父亲）无关。

root: 希腊语 pater（父亲）→ patris（父邦）→ patriotes（同乡）→ 拉丁语 patrioticus → 法语 patriotique → 英语 patriotic，核心义「以父邦为家」。

sensesIntro.en: Patriotic starts as a private love of country, becomes visible in customs and works, and can finally harden into a critical label for nationalism.
sensesIntro.cn: patriotic 先从私人的爱国之情出发，进而外化为习俗与作品，最后可能硬化成批评民族主义的标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person hugging the national flag at sunrise.
core.cn: 核心意象：晨曦中有人紧抱国旗。

branches.en: Private love of the fatherland is the first sense.
branches.cn: 对父邦的私人热爱是第一个义项。

branches.en: Public acts turn the feeling into custom.
branches.cn: 公开行为把情感变成习俗。

branches.en: Songs and poems carry the feeling as works.
branches.cn: 歌曲与诗歌以作品承载情感。

branches.en: Excessive display turns the word into a label.
branches.cn: 过度展示使该词变成标签。

branches.en: Parades and rallies can move from loyalty to criticism.
branches.cn: 游行与集会可能从忠诚滑向被批评的过度展示。

intro.en: Patriotic is built on the root of pater, with noun and adverb members of the same family.
intro.cn: patriotic 建立在 pater 词根上，同族中还有名词与副词成员。

latinIntro.en: Greek and Latin forms of father and fatherland give the base patri-.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语与拉丁语中「父亲、父邦」的词形提供词基 patri-。

items.example: Pater is the Latin word for father.
items.exampleCN: pater 是拉丁语的「父亲」。

items.example: The root patri- starts many English words.
items.exampleCN: 词根 patri- 引出许多英语单词。

items.example: Patris names the land of ones fathers.
items.exampleCN: patris 指祖先之地。

items.meaning: a person who loves his country
items.example: A patriot loves the fatherland.
items.exampleCN: 爱国者热爱父邦。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms patriotic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 构成 patriotic。

items.meaningCN: 具有……性质或主义的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ism forms patriotism.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ism 构成 patriotism。

items.example: The suffix -ally forms patriotically.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ally 构成 patriotically。

items.example: The prefix un- forms unpatriotic.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unpatriotic。

items.example: Patriarchy keeps the father root.
items.exampleCN: patriarchy 保留父亲词根。

definition_zh: 赞助；资助；庇护；惠顾； patronage 式的人事安排； patronage（权力上位者给予的恩惠）
definition_en: the support, money, or privileges that a wealthy or powerful person gives to another
core_image: 一位富有的主人向画家递上一袋钱，并伸手护住画家身后的画架
scene: 文艺复兴时期，画家靠贵族的资助维持画室，也要按主人心意选题材。In the Renaissance, painters kept their studios alive through the patronage of wealthy nobles.
sceneCN: 这里 patronage 是「赞助、资助」（第 1 个义项：有钱有势者对他人提供财物支持）；句意：文艺复兴时期的画家靠贵族的 patronage 维持画室。

pos.zh: 赞助；资助；庇护；惠顾； patronage 式人事安排
（旧用法）恩赐之权；有权给予的职位

collocations.zh: 政治庇护； patronage 式政治分肥
撤回报刊/商家的支持；不再惠顾

derivatives.zh: 赞助人；顾客；源自拉丁语 patronus（保护人）
光顾；以居高临下的态度对待；由 patron 加 -ize
居高临下的；由 patronize 加 -ing
赞助人的；由 patron 加 -al
女赞助人；由 patron 加女性后缀 -ess

senses.title: Financial support for artists and writers
senses.definition: money, commissions, or other support given by a wealthy person or institution so that an artist, writer, or scholar can keep working
senses.definitionCN: 富有者或机构为让艺术家、作家、学者得以继续工作而提供金钱、委托或其他支持
senses.example: The chapel was painted under the patronage of a wealthy merchant.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小礼拜堂是在一位富商的赞助下绘成的。
senses.why: The image of a patron handing over money is the core picture, and it gives the literal sense of funding.
senses.whyCN: 主人递上钱袋的画面就是核心意象，直接给出「出钱支持」的字面义。

senses.title: Protection given by a powerful person
senses.definition: the protection and favour that a powerful person gives to someone, often in return for loyalty
senses.definitionCN: 有权势者给予某人的保护与偏袒，常以忠诚作为回报
senses.example: The young poet gained the patronage of a prince.
senses.exampleCN: 那位年轻诗人得到了亲王的庇护。
senses.why: In Latin a patronus was a protector, so support by money and protection by power share the same root picture.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 patronus 即保护人，因此出钱支持与出力庇护共用同一画面。

senses.title: Custom from regular customers
senses.definition: the regular custom or trade that customers give to a shop, hotel, or business
senses.definitionCN: 顾客对商店、旅馆或企业的经常性光顾与消费
senses.example: Local residents give the family bakery steady patronage.
senses.exampleCN: 当地居民让这家家庭面包房一直有稳定顾客。
senses.why: A patron also means a regular customer, so the money a shop receives in trade becomes patronage.
senses.whyCN: patron 也指老顾客，于是商店在交易中收到的钱就成了 patronage。

senses.title: Jobs and favours handed out for political support
senses.titleCN: 政治分肥； patronage 式人事安排
senses.definition: the practice of giving jobs, contracts, or favours to political supporters, often used with disapproval
senses.definitionCN: 把职位、合同或好处给予政治支持者的做法，常含贬义
senses.example: The mayor was accused of filling city offices through patronage.
senses.exampleCN: 市长被指责通过政治分肥来安插市政职位。
senses.why: From choosing clients, a patron moved to choosing staff, so the same support became a way to reward loyalty with jobs.
senses.whyCN: 保护人从挑选顾客走向挑选职员，同一份支持于是变成用职位奖赏忠诚的手段。

senses.title: Appointment to church offices
senses.definition: the right held by a landowner or crown to appoint the holder of a church living (an old ecclesiastical sense)
senses.definitionCN: 地主或君主推荐任命教堂圣职持有人的权利（旧宗教义）
senses.example: In many villages the squire held the patronage of the parish church.
senses.exampleCN: 在许多村庄，乡绅拥有教区教堂的圣职推荐权。
senses.why: Protection by a powerful person could include choosing who holds an office, so patronage came to mean the right to appoint.
senses.whyCN: 有权者的庇护也包括决定由谁任职，于是 patronage 衍生出任命权之义。

intro.en: Patronage comes from Latin pater through patronus, a protector, and Old French patronage, the office of a protector.
intro.cn: patronage 由拉丁语 pater 出发，经 patronus（保护人）与古法语 patronage（保护人之职）而来。

items.en: Pater means father, the head of a household who shelters his people.
items.cn: pater 意为父亲，是庇护家众的家长。

items.en: Patronus means a protector or legal advocate, from pater, and is used for a former master freeing a slave.
items.cn: patronus 出自 pater，意为保护人、法律上的辩护人，也指释放奴隶的旧主人。

items.en: Patronage names the office or position of a patron.
items.cn: patronage 指赞助人（保护人）的职位或身份。

items.en: Patronage arrives in English through French usage.
items.cn: patronage 经法语用法进入英语。

items.en: The word covers the support of artists and the right to present clergy to a living.
items.cn: 该词既涵盖对艺术家的支持，又指推荐圣职的权利。

items.en: Modern use adds the disapproval sense of jobs given for political support.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了表示「政治分肥」的贬义。

note.en: Patronage belongs to the pater family and stands near words of sponsorship, protection, and favour.
note.cn: patronage 属于 pater 词族，并与「赞助、庇护、恩惠」类词相邻。

entries.definition: a person who supports or regularly uses something
to support a business, or to treat someone in a superior way
entries.definitionCN: 光顾；以居高临下的态度对待

entries.definition: of a father, or fatherly in a protective way
money or support given to an event or person, often with advertising in return
the act of keeping someone safe from harm
an act of kindness or a benefit given to someone

normalIntro.en: Patronage joins the protector noun patron with the suffix of state and act, so it means the support a patron gives.
normalIntro.cn: patronage 由名词 patron（保护人）加表示状态与行为的名词后缀构成，意为保护人所给的支持。

normal.en: Drop the -age and you have patron, the person who gives the support.
normal.cn: 去掉 -age 就是 patron，即提供支持的人。

normal.en: Patronize is the verb, used for shopping as well as for looking down on someone.
normal.cn: 动词 patronize 既用于光顾商店，也用于表示居高临下。

normal.en: Under the patronage of is the standard phrase for sponsored events.
normal.cn: under the patronage of 是表示赞助的标准说法。

normal.en: Political patronage is the common critical phrase for jobs given to supporters.
normal.cn: political patronage 是描述「任人唯亲、分肥」的常用批评说法。

normal.en: Use with caution: outside arts and charity, patronage often sounds negative.
normal.cn: 留意义褒贬：在艺术与慈善之外，patronage 常带负面意味。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy hand resting on a painting, and a purse placed beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只厚重的手搭在油画上，旁边放着一只钱袋。

abstract.en: Imagine a prince opening a door so a young poet may walk through.
abstract.cn: 想象一位亲王推开一扇门，让年轻诗人走进去。

abstract.en: Think of a small shop with one loyal family walking in every Sunday.
abstract.cn: 想象一家小店，每周日都有同一家人准时走进来。

examples.en: The museum was founded under royal patronage.
examples.cn: 这座博物馆是在王室赞助下建立的。

examples.en: Critics say the reforms replaced ability with political patronage.
examples.cn: 批评者说这些改革让政治分肥取代了能力。

examples.en: The theatre depends on the patronage of local families.
examples.cn: 这家剧院依赖当地家族的资助。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派」+「戳」+「牛」+「治」——主人「派」人给画师「戳」上印章，画面牛气；这只是拆音联想，与词源（patronus 保护人）无关。

root: 拉丁语 pater（父亲）→ patronus（保护人、辩护人）→ 古法语 patronage（赞助人之职）→ 英语 patronage，核心义「像父亲一样护住并养着别人」。

sensesIntro.en: Patronage begins as money given by a powerful protector, grows into protection and regular custom, and can sour into jobs handed to supporters.
sensesIntro.cn: patronage 先指权势者的出钱支持，再扩展为庇护与经常光顾，最后可能贬化为把职位派给支持者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a patron passing a purse and shielding the work behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：赞助人递出钱袋，并护住身后的作品。

branches.en: Funding for the arts is the literal core sense.
branches.cn: 资助艺术是字面核心义项。

branches.en: Protection by a powerful person grew from the protector root.
branches.cn: 有权者的庇护出自保护人词根。

branches.en: Regular custom is the everyday shop sense.
branches.cn: 经常光顾是商店日常义项。

branches.en: Jobs given to supporters are the critical modern sense.
branches.cn: 把工作给支持者是现代批评义项。

branches.en: Funding and protection were usually handed out together.
branches.cn: 资助与庇护往往同时给予。

intro.en: Patronage is patron plus the state-and-act suffix -age, within a family built on the root of pater.
intro.cn: patronage 是 patron 加表示状态与行为的后缀 -age，整个词族则建立在 pater 词根上。

latinIntro.en: Latin pater, patronus, and patronaticus supply the forms behind the English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pater、patronus、patronaticus 提供这套英语词族的词形来源。

items.example: Pater gives the sense of a protecting head.
items.exampleCN: pater 提供「家长式保护者」的意味。

items.example: Patronus is the source of patron.
items.exampleCN: patronus 是 patron 的来源。

items.example: A patron funds the work.
items.exampleCN: 赞助人出资支持作品。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态、集合或行为的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -age forms patronage.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -age 构成 patronage。

items.example: The suffix -ize forms patronize.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 构成 patronize。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms patronizing.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 patronizing。

items.example: The suffix -al forms patronal.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 构成 patronal。

items.example: The suffix -ess forms patroness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ess 构成 patroness。

items.example: Paternal keeps the father sense plainly.
items.exampleCN: paternal 直接保留父亲之义。

definition_zh: 少量；缺乏；不足
definition_en: the state of having too few of something, so that there is not enough
core_image: 一只大碗里只剩几粒米，碗底几乎照得出光
scene: 荒年过后，村里讨论粮食储备时只看到几袋袋口敞开。After the bad harvest, the village council admitted a paucity of grain in the shared store.
sceneCN: 这里 paucity 是「不足、匮乏」（第 1 个义项：某种东西数量太少）；句意：歉收之后，村议会承认公共粮仓里的粮食十分匮乏。

derivatives.zh: 穷人；源自拉丁语 pauper（贫穷的）
（语言学）表示少量的；如少数格
使贫穷；由 pauper 加 -ize 构成
（仅作说明）词用得太少的说法

senses.title: Having too few of something
senses.definition: the condition of having fewer of something than is needed
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的数量比所需要的少
senses.example: There is a paucity of evidence for the claim.
senses.exampleCN: 这一说法缺乏证据。
senses.why: From Latin paucus, meaning few, the word starts with plain lack, an empty bowl rather than an abstract problem.
senses.whyCN: 出自拉丁语 paucus（少），词义从最朴素的缺乏开始，是一只空碗而非抽象问题。

senses.title: Scarcity in a written account
senses.definition: a noticeable shortage of details or examples in an account, report, or argument
senses.definitionCN: 记载、报告或论证中细节或例子的明显稀少
senses.example: The report is clear but suffers from a paucity of detail.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告条理清楚，但细节太少。
senses.why: A shortage can also be counted inside a text, where too few examples leave the page thin.
senses.whyCN: 短缺也可以落在文本内部：例子太少，页面自然显得单薄。

senses.title: A formal word for scarcity
senses.definition: a formal noun, common in academic and legal writing, used for an insufficiency that may be argued or measured
senses.definitionCN: 学术与法律写作中常见的正式名词，指可被论证或测量的不足
senses.example: The paper opens by noting the paucity of comparable studies.
senses.exampleCN: 论文开篇指出可供比较的研究十分匮乏。
senses.why: Shortage needs a careful word in academic writing, so the noun takes on a formal tone there.
senses.whyCN: 学术写作需要谨慎的措辞来表达短缺，这个名词因此带上正式语气。

intro.en: Paucity comes from Latin paucitas, from paucus, meaning few.
intro.cn: paucity 来自拉丁语 paucitas，其词根 paucus 意为「少的」。

items.en: Paucus means few or little in number.
items.cn: paucus 意为数量上的「少」。

items.en: Paucitas means fewness or scarcity.
items.cn: paucitas 意为稀少、匮乏。

items.en: Printing writers used paucitas for scarcity in Latin prose.
items.cn: 十五世纪拉丁语散文用 paucitas 表示匮乏。

items.en: Paucity enters English as a formal noun for shortage.
items.cn: paucity 在十五、十六世纪进入英语，是表示匮乏的正式名词。

items.en: The word settles mostly in academic writing about evidence and data.
items.cn: 现代英语中它多用于学术写作，谈论证据与数据。

items.en: Paucity becomes common in criticism and statistical reports.
items.cn: 到十九、二十世纪，它在评论与统计报告中变得常见。

note.en: Paucity looks like poverty and shares a Latin sense of smallness with a few words about shortage.
note.cn: paucity 与 poverty 形近，并和几个表示「短缺」的词共享拉丁语的「小、少」概念。

entries.definition: the state of being poor; only similar in spelling, different in origin
entries.definitionCN: 贫穷；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a grammatical form meaning a few
entries.definitionCN: 少量数；同用 paucus 词根

entries.definition: a very poor person; from Latin pauper, a different root of poverty
entries.definitionCN: 穷人；源自 pauper，与贫穷同源，非本词词根

entries.definition: a shortage of something that is needed
an inadequate supply of something
a lack of something that is needed

normalIntro.en: Paucity hides the Latin word for few inside it, so think of everything shrinking to a handful.
normalIntro.cn: paucity 内含拉丁语的「少」，可以想成所有东西缩成一把。

normal.en: The root pauc- means few, as in paucus, little.
normal.cn: 词根 pauc- 意为少，如同 paucus（少的）。

normal.en: The suffix -ity makes an abstract noun of state, like scarcity and rarity.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ity 使它为抽象状态名词，如同 scarcity、rarity。

normal.en: The phrase a paucity of usually needs a noun of evidence, data, or detail.
normal.cn: a paucity of 后常接 evidence、data、detail 等名词。

normal.en: Scarcity is the everyday partner, so paucity sounds more formal.
normal.cn: scarcity 是日常同义词，paucity 更正式。

normal.en: In IELTS writing, a paucity of data is a useful precise phrase.
normal.cn: 在雅思写作中，a paucity of data 是可用的精确表达。

abstract.en: Picture an empty bowl set before a large family.
abstract.cn: 想象一只空碗摆在一大家人面前。

abstract.en: Imagine a notebook page with a single line written on it.
abstract.cn: 想象笔记本上一整页只写了一行字。

abstract.en: Think of a long meeting that ends with very few concrete sentences in the minutes.
abstract.cn: 想象一场漫长的会议，纪要里却只有寥寥几句具体内容。

examples.en: The study was abandoned because of a paucity of data.
examples.cn: 这项研究因数据匮乏而中止。

examples.en: There is a paucity of affordable housing in the city centre.
examples.cn: 市中心可负担的住房十分匮乏。

examples.en: His essay is neat, but a paucity of examples weakens the argument.
examples.cn: 他的文章整洁，但例子太少削弱了论证。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「跑」+「city」——「跑」遍了整座城也买不到，就是资源太少；这只是拆音联想，与词源（paucus 少的）无关。

root: 拉丁语 paucus（少的）→ paucitas（稀少）→ 英语 paucity，核心义「少得不够用」。

sensesIntro.en: Paucity begins with simple lack from Latin for few, then moves to sparse detail and to the formal register of scarcity.
sensesIntro.cn: paucity 从拉丁语「少」带来的朴素缺乏出发，再指细节稀少，最后落到正式的「匮乏」语域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty bowl with only a few grains left.
core.cn: 核心意象：只剩下几粒米的大碗。

branches.en: Plain lack is the base sense.
branches.cn: 朴素的缺乏是基础义项。

branches.en: Sparse detail applies the lack to a record.
branches.cn: 细节稀少把缺乏用于记载。

branches.en: The formal register frames the lack for academic writing.
branches.cn: 正式语域把这一缺乏用于学术写作。

branches.en: Both empty arguments about evidence and thin accounts are paucity of detail.
branches.cn: 证据不足的论证与单薄的记载都是细节匮乏。

branches.en: A formal report gains power when it measures a paucity of detail.
branches.cn: 正式报告在衡量细节匮乏时更有说服力。

intro.en: Paucity is the Latin root pauc- for few plus -ity, a suffix for abstract states, extended to a few related forms.
intro.cn: paucity 是表示「少」的拉丁词根 pauc- 加抽象状态后缀 -ity，并延伸出几个相关词形。

latinIntro.en: Latin paucus and paucitas carry the idea of few, with paucalis marking a few in grammar.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 paucus 与 paucitas 承载「少」的观念，paucalis 在语法上表示少量。

items.example: Paucus gives the root pauc-.
items.exampleCN: paucus 提供词根 pauc-。

items.example: Paucus as a noun means a few.
items.exampleCN: paucus 作名词意为少数人。

items.example: The root pauc- starts paucity.
items.exampleCN: 词根 pauc- 引出 paucity。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ity forms paucity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 paucity。

items.example: The suffix -al forms paucal.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 构成 paucal。

items.example: Paucal keeps the root meaning.
items.exampleCN: paucal 保留词根含义。

items.example: Pauper is a related Latin form for the poor.
items.exampleCN: pauper 是相关的拉丁贫穷词形。

items.example: The suffix -ize forms pauperize.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 构成 pauperize。

items.example: The suffix -ity is repeated for scarcity.
items.exampleCN: 表示状态的 -ity 也出现在 scarcity 中。

definition_zh: 人行道；路面；铺过的地面
definition_en: a hard surface laid for walking, especially a path beside a road
core_image: 工匠把一块块石板砸实，铺成一条平整的硬路
scene: 早晨的街道上，行人走在石板铺成的人行道上。In the morning street, people are walking on the pavement.
sceneCN: 这里 pavement 是「人行道」（第 1 个义项：供人步行的铺砌路面）；句意：早晨的街道上，行人走在石板铺成的人行道上。

collocations.zh: 人行道上的露天咖啡座

derivatives.zh: 由名词去掉后附成分回生的动词，义为「铺砌」
动词 pave 加 -ing 构成，义为「铺路材料；铺装」
pave 加表示施动者的 -or 构成，义为「铺路工；铺路砖」

senses.title: A walkway beside a road
senses.definition: the hard path beside a road where people walk
senses.definitionCN: 道路旁边供行人步行的硬质路面
senses.example: She waited on the pavement outside the bank.
senses.exampleCN: 她在银行外面的人行道上等着。
senses.why: The Old French verb paves, meaning to pave, plus -ment for the result, so the word first names what paving leaves behind: a hard surface to walk on.
senses.whyCN: 古法语动词 pave 意为「铺设」，加 -ment 表示结果，所以这个词先指铺砌后留下的、可供行走的硬面。

senses.title: The paved surface of a road
senses.definition: the layer of stones, bricks, or concrete that forms a road or courtyard
senses.definitionCN: 由石块、砖或混凝土构成的道路或庭院的表层
senses.example: Cracks in the pavement let the rain seep through.
senses.exampleCN: 路面上的裂缝让雨水渗了下去。
senses.why: If paving produces a walking surface, the same surface that carries wheels is also called pavement, so the sense widens from feet to traffic.
senses.whyCN: 既然铺设产生供人行走的表面，同一表面承载车轮时也叫 pavement，于是义项从「脚下」扩展到「车行」。

senses.title: A floor of stone or tile
senses.definition: a floor covered with stone or tiles, often in a yard or square
senses.definitionCN: 用石块或瓷砖铺成的地面，多见于庭院或广场
senses.example: The mosaic pavement of the old villa is still visible.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老别墅的马赛克地面至今仍可见。
senses.why: The paving image is not tied to streets, so any hard floor laid in pieces can take the name, from Roman villas to mosque courtyards.
senses.whyCN: 铺砌的意象并不限于街道，因此任何以块材铺成的硬地面都能用这个名字，从罗马别墅到清真寺庭院皆然。

senses.title: Soil covered with a crust
senses.definition: a hard layer of soil or sand that forms a crust on the ground
senses.definitionCN: 在地面上形成的坚硬土壳或沙壳
senses.example: A dark pavement of baked mud covered the plain.
senses.exampleCN: 平原上覆盖着一层被晒硬的深色土壳。
senses.why: The technical sense borrows the idea of a laid hard layer and applies it to nature, where sun or salt forms a crust.
senses.whyCN: 专业义借用「铺设硬层」的想法，用于自然界中由日晒或盐分形成的硬壳。

intro.en: Pavement comes from Latin pavimentum, a beaten floor, through Old French paviment.
intro.cn: pavement 来自拉丁语 pavimentum（夯实的铺地），经古法语 paviment 进入英语。

items.en: Pavimentum means a floor of stone or earth that has been beaten down.
items.cn: pavimentum 意为用石块或泥土夯实的铺地。

items.en: The verb pavire, to beat or ram down, is generally taken as the source of pavimentum.
items.cn: 一般认为动词 pavire（捶打、夯实）是 pavimentum 的来源。

items.en: Paviment carries the Latin noun into French.
items.cn: paviment 把拉丁名词带入法语。

items.en: Pavement first appears in English for a paved floor.
items.cn: pavement 在英语中最早指铺砌的地面。

items.en: British use shifts the word to the raised footway beside a road.
items.cn: 英式用法把该词转到道路旁垫高的人行道上。

items.en: American English keeps pavement for road surfaces, so the walkway is called sidewalk.
items.cn: 美式英语保留 pavement 指路面，人行道另称 sidewalk。

note.en: Pavement is the noun of paving results, next to pave, paving, and to the walkway words that differ by region.
note.cn: pavement 是表示「铺设结果」的名词，与 pave、paving 相邻，也与因地区而异的「人行道」词族相邻。

entries.definition: to cover a surface with stones or bricks
the material or act of covering a surface
a light building in a park or garden
entries.definitionCN: 亭子；只是开头拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a paved path beside a road
a path for people to walk on
the part of a road used by traffic

normalIntro.en: Pavement is the flat result of paving: Latin pavimentum named a floor that was rammed down hard.
normalIntro.cn: pavement 是「铺设」留下的平整结果：拉丁语 pavimentum 指被夯实的硬地面。

normal.en: The verb pave and the noun pavement share the Latin root pavimentum.
normal.cn: 动词 pave 与名词 pavement 共享拉丁词根 pavimentum。

normal.en: The -ment ending marks a result, so pavement is the paved thing.
normal.cn: 结尾 -ment 表示结果，所以 pavement 就是铺好的东西。

normal.en: In British English you wait for a bus on the pavement.
normal.cn: 英式英语中，在「人行道」上等公交车说 on the pavement。

normal.en: In American English the same path is the sidewalk.
normal.cn: 美式英语中，同样的道路旁人行道叫 sidewalk。

normal.en: A pavement artist draws pictures on the ground with chalk.
normal.cn: pavement artist 是用粉笔在路面作画的街头画家。

abstract.en: Picture stone slabs hammered flat until the surface rings under a boot.
abstract.cn: 想象石板被锤得平整，靴子踩上去发出清脆回声。

abstract.en: Think of a long grey ribbon of footway running beside a busy street.
abstract.cn: 想象一条灰色的人行道紧贴着繁忙的马路延伸。

abstract.en: Imagine a tiled floor in an old villa shining under a lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象老别墅里铺砖的地面在灯下泛着光。

examples.en: Children were chalking shapes on the pavement outside the shop.
examples.cn: 孩子们在店外人行道上用粉笔画着图案。

examples.en: The old pavements in this town were laid with river stones.
examples.cn: 这个镇上的旧人行道是用河石铺成的。

examples.en: He stepped off the road onto the pavement and waited for the light.
examples.cn: 他从马路上走到人行道上，等着信号灯。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「僻服门」——巷子拐角铺出一条平整的路，供人绕进小门；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pavire（捶打、夯实）→ pavimentum（夯实的铺地）→ 古法语 paviment → 英语 pavement，核心义「夯平铺好的硬面」；pavire 与 pavimentum 的关系一般认为如此，细节仍有讨论。

sensesIntro.en: Pavement begins with a laid hard floor, then narrows to the path beside a road, widens to road surfaces, and finally lends its image to natural crusts.
sensesIntro.cn: pavement 从「铺好的硬地面」出发，先收窄到道路旁的人行道，再扩展到路面，最后把「硬壳」的意象借给自然地貌。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: stone slabs hammered flat into a walking surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：石板被锤平，铺成可走的硬面。

branches.en: The footway sense is the everyday British one.
branches.cn: 人行道义是英式英语中最日常的用法。

branches.en: Road surfaces and tiled floors both keep the laid surface image.
branches.cn: 路面与铺砖地面都保留了「铺设表面」的意象。

branches.en: Both a walkway and a soil crust are thin hard layers at ground level.
branches.cn: 人行道与土壳都是贴地的一层硬表皮。

branches.en: The traffic sense differs from the walkway sense only in who uses the surface.
branches.cn: 车行路面义与步行义的区别只在于使用这层表面的对象不同。

branches.en: All three concrete senses share one origin in Latin pavimentum.
branches.cn: 三个具体义项同出于拉丁语 pavimentum 这一来源。

intro.en: Pavement is built from the Latin stem pav-, seen in pavimentum, plus the French ending -ment that names a result.
intro.cn: pavement 由拉丁词干 pav-（见 pavimentum）加表示结果的法语词尾 -ment 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin pavimentum means a beaten floor, and the related verb pavire means to beat or ram down.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pavimentum 意为夯实的铺地，相关动词 pavire 意为捶打、夯实。

items.meaning: a floor of stone or earth
items.example: Pavimentum is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: pavimentum 是直接的拉丁语来源。

items.example: Pavire supplies the hammering image.
items.exampleCN: pavire 提供「夯实」的意象。

items.example: Pavimentar is the French verb of paving.
items.exampleCN: pavimentar 是法语中的「铺设」动词。

items.meaningCN: 表示结果或产物的词尾
items.example: The ending -ment marks a result.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ment 标记结果。

items.example: Pave is the short English verb.
items.exampleCN: pave 是简短的英语动词。

items.example: Paving is the action and the material.
items.exampleCN: paving 既指动作也指材料。

items.example: Pavior adds the -or suffix for actors.
items.exampleCN: pavior 加 -or 表示施动者。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms paving.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 paving。

items.example: Pavement keeps the floor sense.
items.exampleCN: pavement 保留「地面」之义。

definition_zh: 亭子；展馆；帐篷；大型场馆
definition_en: a light building with an open side, used for shelter, shows, or events
core_image: 公园草坪上一座四面敞开的轻巧亭子，尖顶像张开的大翅
scene: 周末公园里，人们坐在亭子下躲雨聊天。On a weekend in the park, people sit under the pavilion to chat and stay out of the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 pavilion 是「亭子」（第 1 个义项：公园里供人歇脚、敞开的轻便建筑）；句意：周末公园里，人们坐在亭子下躲雨聊天。

pos.zh: 亭子；展馆；帐篷；大型场馆

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 papilio（蝴蝶）派生，义为「蝶形的」，与蝴蝶的翅膀同源
pavilion 加 roof 构成的复合名词，义为「四坡顶」
同源拉丁名词，义为「蝴蝶」，是 pavilion 蝴蝶意象的来源

senses.title: A light open shelter in a park
senses.definition: a small light building with open sides, often in a garden or park
senses.definitionCN: 常建于园林或公园中、一侧或多侧敞开的轻便小建筑
senses.example: An old wooden pavilion stood beside the pond.
senses.exampleCN: 池塘边立着一座古老的木亭。
senses.why: Old French pavillon meant a large decorated tent shaped like a butterfly wing, so the name first belonged to a light structure that could be erected quickly.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 pavillon 原指形似蝴蝶翅的大帐篷，所以这个名字最初属于可快速搭起的轻便建筑。

senses.title: A stand at an exhibition
senses.definition: a separate building or block where goods or arts are shown
senses.definitionCN: 在博览会或展览中单独建起、用于陈列展品的建筑或展区
senses.example: The flower pavilion drew long queues all day.
senses.exampleCN: 花卉展馆一整天都排着长队。
senses.why: A fair used to be a field of tents, and each stall kept the old tent name, which survives in the modern fairground pavilion.
senses.whyCN: 旧时集市就是一片帐篷，每个摊位沿用旧时的帐篷之名，这一用法就保留在现代展馆上。

senses.title: A large ornate tent
senses.definition: a large tent, often decorated, used for outdoor ceremonies
senses.definitionCN: 用于户外典礼的大型装饰帐篷
senses.example: The king entered the field under a crimson pavilion.
senses.exampleCN: 国王在深红色的华盖帐篷下进入场地。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer of meaning, since the French word named the rounded field tent of an army or a royal court.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的词义层，因为法语词原指军队或宫廷用的圆形野营大帐。

senses.title: A sports ground building
senses.definition: a building at a sports ground for players, officials, or spectators
senses.definitionCN: 运动场旁供运动员、工作人员或观众使用的建筑
senses.example: The cricket team left the pavilion after lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 板球队午饭后离开了球场休息楼。
senses.why: From a tent set up at a match, the word grew to a permanent building serving a playing field.
senses.whyCN: 从赛场上临时搭起的帐篷，这个词扩展到为运动场地服务的固定建筑。

intro.en: Pavilion comes through Old French pavillon from Latin papilio, a butterfly, so named for the wing-like sweeping shape of a large tent.
intro.cn: pavilion 经古法语 pavillon 来自拉丁语 papilio（蝴蝶），因大帐篷两翼舒展如蝶翅而得名。

items.en: Papilio means butterfly, and Late Latin papilio also names a tent.
items.cn: papilio 意为蝴蝶，晚期拉丁语中又指帐篷。

items.en: Pavillon names a large round or square tent of a court.
items.cn: pavillon 指宫廷使用的大型圆帐或方帐。

items.en: Pavilion enters English for an ornamental tent, and soon for a garden building.
items.cn: pavilion 进入英语时指装饰性帐篷，随后指园中建筑。

items.en: Garden pavilions become fashionable in parks and large houses.
items.cn: 园林凉亭在公园与大宅中变得流行。

items.en: World fairs give the word its modern exhibition sense.
items.cn: 万国博览会赋予该词现代「展馆」之义。

items.en: Modern English uses pavilion for sports buildings and hospital wings.
items.cn: 现代英语用 pavilion 指体育场建筑和医院分楼。

note.en: Pavilion belongs to the butterfly-tent family and sits beside other small buildings for shelter or display.
note.cn: pavilion 属于「蝶翅帐篷」词族，也与其它供休憩或展示的小型建筑相邻。

entries.definition: Latin for butterfly
shaped like a butterfly
a paved walking surface
entries.definitionCN: 铺砌的路面；只是开头拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a small roofed summerhouse in a garden
a small stand at a market or fair
a small open structure at a public place

normalIntro.en: Pavilion is a butterfly word: Latin papilio and the French tent pavillon share one sweeping shape.
normalIntro.cn: pavilion 是一只「蝴蝶」词：拉丁语 papilio 与法语帐篷 pavillon 共享舒展的外形。

normal.en: The base papilio means butterfly in Latin.
normal.cn: 词干 papilio 在拉丁语中意为蝴蝶。

normal.en: A large tent with two spread wings looked like a butterfly.
normal.cn: 两翼张开的大帐篷看上去像一只蝴蝶。

normal.en: A garden pavilion is an open-sided shelter for hot summer days.
normal.cn: 园林凉亭是盛夏时节四面敞开的乘凉处。

normal.en: At a world fair, each country builds its own exhibition pavilion.
normal.cn: 在世博会上，每个国家都建自己的展馆。

normal.en: Compare gazebo: both are garden shelters, but gazebo is usually small and octagonal.
normal.cn: 对比 gazebo：两者都是园中亭，但 gazebo 多指八角小亭。

abstract.en: Picture a giant white tent whose two wings fold out like butterfly wings.
abstract.cn: 想象一顶巨大的白色帐篷，两翼像蝶翅一样展开。

abstract.en: Imagine sitting on the steps of an open pavilion while rain drums on the roof.
abstract.cn: 想象坐在开敞亭子的台阶上，听雨点敲打屋顶。

abstract.en: Think of a fairground where every flag marks another pavilion.
abstract.cn: 想象博览会上一面面旗子标出一个个展馆。

examples.en: The wedding ceremony was held in a white pavilion on the lawn.
examples.cn: 婚礼在草坪上的白色大帐篷里举行。

examples.en: Visitors queued for an hour to enter the science pavilion.
examples.cn: 参观者排队一个多小时才进入科学展馆。

examples.en: Pigeons gathered under the stone pavilion at the courtyard corner.
examples.cn: 鸽子聚集在庭院角落的石亭下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕围帘」——亭子有时要挂起围帘遮阳，怕人挡了风；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 papilio（蝴蝶）→ 晚期拉丁语 papilio（帐篷）→ 古法语 pavillon（大帐篷）→ 英语 pavilion（帐篷；亭子；展馆），核心义「形如蝶翅张开的轻便建筑」。

sensesIntro.en: Pavilion starts as a tent shaped like butterfly wings, becomes a garden shelter, and then extends to exhibition musters and sports buildings.
sensesIntro.cn: pavilion 从形似蝶翅的帐篷出发，变为园林亭子，再延伸到展览建筑与体育场建筑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a light building whose roof spreads like butterfly wings.
core.cn: 核心意象：屋顶如蝶翅舒展的轻巧建筑。

branches.en: The garden shelter is the most familiar modern sense.
branches.cn: 园林亭子是最熟悉的现代义项。

branches.en: The decorated tent keeps the oldest layer of the word.
branches.cn: 装饰大帐篷保留了最古老的词义层。

branches.en: Exhibition halls and sports buildings both extend the tent into a permanent structure.
branches.cn: 展馆与体育场建筑都把帐篷扩展为固定建筑。

branches.en: A garden pavilion is a tent turned into landscape architecture.
branches.cn: 园林凉亭就是被景观化的帐篷。

branches.en: All four senses describe a light open building for people to gather under.
branches.cn: 四个义项都指供人聚集在其下的轻便敞开建筑。

intro.en: Pavilion is a loanword whose core sits in the Latin noun papilio, with -ion and French -on endings shaping the modern form.
intro.cn: pavilion 是借词，其核心来自拉丁名词 papilio，现代拼写则受 -ion 与法语 -on 影响。

latinIntro.en: Latin papilio means butterfly, and Late Latin extended it to a tent.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 papilio 意为蝴蝶，晚期拉丁语又把它扩展为帐篷。

items.example: Papilio is the Latin source of the word.
items.exampleCN: papilio 是该词的拉丁语来源。

items.example: The stem papilion- appears in botanical names.
items.exampleCN: 词干 papilion- 见于植物学名称。

items.example: Pavillon carries the word into French.
items.exampleCN: pavillon 把该词带入法语。

items.example: The ending -ion fixes the English noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 固定了英语名词形式。

items.example: The French ending -on shortens the Latin form.
items.exampleCN: 法语词尾 -on 缩短了拉丁形式。

items.example: Papilionaceous plants have butterfly-like flowers.
items.exampleCN: 蝶形花植物的花像蝴蝶。

items.meaning: a roof sloping on all four sides
items.example: The pavilion roof slopes on every side.
items.exampleCN: 四坡顶四面倾斜。

items.example: Pavilion keeps the tent image.
items.exampleCN: pavilion 保留帐篷的意象。

definition_zh: 应付的；到期支付的；可支付的
definition_en: that must be paid, or that can legally be paid
core_image: 账单上有一行到期日，到了那天钱必须交出去
scene: 财务桌上放着一张账单，上面写着付款的最后期限。On the finance desk lies a bill with a final date by which the amount is payable.
sceneCN: 这里 payable 是「应付的、到期支付的」（第 1 个义项：到期应当支付的款项）；句意：财务桌上放着一张账单，上面写着付款的最后期限。

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，义为「支付」；payable 由它加后缀构成
pay 加 -ment 构成，义为「付款；支付款项」
pay 加表示施动者的 -er 构成，义为「付款人」
pay 加表示承受者的 -ee 构成，义为「收款人」，与 payable 中的 -able 同表「可被……的」

senses.title: Due to be paid
senses.definition: that must be paid, especially by a stated date
senses.definitionCN: 必须支付的，尤指按规定日期支付的
senses.example: The remaining balance is payable within thirty days.
senses.exampleCN: 剩余余额须在三十天内付清。
senses.why: The suffix -able marks what can or must be done to something, so what can be paid is also what owes payment.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -able 表示「可以或必须被……的」，所以「可以被支付的东西」也就是「欠着款的东西」。

senses.title: Legally able to be paid
senses.definition: allowed by law to be used or exchanged for payment
senses.definitionCN: 法律上允许用于支付或兑换成现金的
senses.example: Bank notes are payable on demand at the issuing bank.
senses.exampleCN: 纸币可在发行银行见票兑换为现金。
senses.why: Money is described as payable when it can validly be handed over, which is the power side of the same suffix.
senses.whyCN: 货币被称为 payable，指的是它可以合法地被交出去，这是同一词尾「能力」的一面。

senses.title: A debt owed on accounts
senses.definition: money owed by a business and recorded as a liability
senses.definitionCN: 企业欠下并记作负债的款项
senses.example: Accounts payable rose sharply after the big purchase.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔大采购之后，应付账款大幅上升。
senses.why: Accounting turns the adjective into a plural noun, naming the sums that carry the payable label in the books.
senses.whyCN: 会计把这形容词名词化，指账簿上被贴上「应付」标签的那些金额。

intro.en: Payable is a home-built English word: the verb pay plus the suffix -able, modelled on French paiable.
intro.cn: payable 是英语利用 pay 加 -able 构成的词，形式参照法语 paiable。

items.en: Pacare, to make peaceful, gives the French verb payer its root in the sense of settling a quarrel with money.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pacare（使平静）为法语动词 payer 提供词根，其含义是「用钱平息纠纷」。

items.en: Paiier means to satisfy or to pay a debt.
items.cn: paiier 意为使满足或偿还债务。

items.en: Pay enters English from French and soon means to hand over money.
items.cn: pay 经法语进入英语，很快表示「交付钱款」。

items.en: Paiable is the French adjective for what is to be paid.
items.cn: paiable 是法语中表示「应支付的」形容词。

items.en: Payable appears as the English form of that adjective.
items.cn: payable 作为该法语形容词的英语形式出现。

items.en: Commerce makes payable a standard label on bills and ledgers.
items.cn: 商业活动使 payable 成为账单与账簿上的标准用语。

note.en: Payable is one of the -able family of pay, and sits beside the money words that describe debts and ways to settle them.
note.cn: payable 属于 pay 的 -able 词族，与描述债务和付款方式的钱款词相邻。

entries.definition: to give money for something
the person who receives money
the person who pays
the day on which wages are paid
owed and required to be paid now
not yet paid
that is to be received as money owed to you
entries.definitionCN: 应收的；与 payable 相对

normalIntro.en: Payable is pay plus -able: money that can and must be paid over.
normalIntro.cn: payable 就是 pay 加 -able：可以而且必须交出去的钱。

normal.en: The verb pay plus -able gives the adjective payable.
normal.cn: 动词 pay 加 -able 构成形容词 payable。

normal.en: A cheque made payable to a name can only be paid to that person.
normal.cn: 写明 payable to 某个名字的支票，只能付给那个人。

normal.en: Accounts payable lists what a company still owes.
normal.cn: accounts payable 列出公司还欠的钱。

normal.en: Payable contrasts with receivable, which is money owed to you.
normal.cn: payable 与 receivable 相对，后者是别人欠你的钱。

normal.en: Compare due: due stresses the date, payable stresses the obligation to pay.
normal.cn: 对比 due：due 强调日期，payable 强调必须支付的义务。

abstract.en: Picture a red stamp on a bill reading payable at once.
abstract.cn: 想象账单上盖着一枚红章，写着「应立即付款」。

abstract.en: Imagine a bank note that promises to pay the bearer on demand.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸币，上面写着见票即付给持票人。

abstract.en: Think of two columns in a ledger, one owed out and one owed in.
abstract.cn: 想一账簿的两栏：一栏是欠出去的，一栏是收进来的。

examples.en: The rent is payable at the start of each month.
examples.cn: 房租须在每月月初支付。

examples.en: Make the cheque payable to the school, not to me.
examples.cn: 请把支票开给学校，而不是开给我。

examples.en: Accounts payable at the end of the year were higher than expected.
examples.cn: 年末的应付账款比预期更高。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「赔」——要赔的钱当然就是必须付出去的钱；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pacare（使平静，后指缴款平息纠纷）→ 古法语 paiier（支付）→ 英语 pay → pay + -able（可……的）→ payable，核心义「可以被交付的钱」。

sensesIntro.en: Payable begins as what must be paid, then names what may legally be paid, and finally becomes an accounting noun for debts.
sensesIntro.cn: payable 先是「必须支付的」，再指「法律上可以支付的」，最后成为会计中表示债务的名词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bill with a due date stamped in red.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张盖着红色到期章的账单。

branches.en: What must be paid is the ordinary commercial sense.
branches.cn: 必须支付是日常商业义项。

branches.en: What may lawfully be paid is the power sense of the suffix.
branches.cn: 法律上可以支付是词尾「能力」的一面。

branches.en: The accounting noun turns the debt into a book entry.
branches.cn: 会计名词把债务变成账簿上的记录。

branches.en: A due bill and an accounts payable entry name the same obligation.
branches.cn: 到期账单与应付账款记录指的是同一笔义务。

branches.en: Both obligation and permission come from the same -able ending.
branches.cn: 义务与许可都来自同一个 -able 词尾。

intro.en: Payable is pay plus the Latin derived -able, which means able to be or that must be.
intro.cn: payable 由 pay 加源自拉丁语的 -able 构成，意为「可以被……的」或「必须被……的」。

latinIntro.en: Latin pacare means to make peaceful, and its French descendant paiier means to pay.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pacare 意为使平静，其在法语中的后裔 paiier 意为支付。

items.example: Pacare gives the root idea of settling.
items.exampleCN: pacare 提供「平息」的词根义。

items.example: Pax stands behind pacare.
items.exampleCN: pax 是 pacare 的词源基础。

items.example: Paiier carries the sense into French.
items.exampleCN: paiier 把此义带入法语。

items.example: Pay is the short English base.
items.exampleCN: pay 是简短的英语基础词。

items.example: The suffix -able forms payable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 payable。

items.example: The suffix -ment forms payment.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ment 构成 payment。

items.example: The suffix -er forms payer.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 payer。

items.example: The suffix -ee forms payee.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ee 构成 payee。

items.example: Receivable mirrors payable with another base.
items.exampleCN: receivable 换了一个词根与 payable 相对。

definition_zh: 孔雀（尤指雄孔雀）；爱炫耀的人；炫耀；炫耀行为
definition_en: a large male bird with a long train of blue-green feathers with eyespots, or a person who shows off
core_image: 屏风状的尾羽打开，上百只蓝色眼斑一起展开
scene: 植物园的草坪上，围栏里的人纷纷举起手机，一只孔雀把尾屏完全打开了。On the lawn of the botanical garden, visitors raised their phones as a peacock spread its full tail.
sceneCN: 这里 peacock 是「孔雀」（第 1 个义项：尾羽华丽的雄性大鸟）；句意：植物园草坪上，游客们举起手机，因为一只孔雀把尾屏完全展开了。

pos.zh: 孔雀（尤指雄孔雀）；爱炫耀的人

collocations.zh: 鹤立鸡群的人；在一群人里格外醒目的人

derivatives.zh: 雌孔雀；由 pea（由 peacock 缩略而来）+ hen（母鸡）构成，对应雄性的 peacock
小孔雀；由 pea（peacock 的缩略）+ chick（雏鸟）构成
孔雀（统称）；由 pea（peacock 的缩略）+ fowl（禽鸟）构成，不分雌雄
爱炫耀的；像孔雀一样招摇的，由 peacock 加形容词后缀 -ish 构成

senses.title: The blue-green bird with a huge train
senses.definition: a large male peafowl, especially the Indian species, with blue-green plumage and a train edged with eyespots
senses.definitionCN: 一种大型雄性雉类禽鸟，尤指蓝孔雀，羽毛蓝绿，尾羽展开时布满眼斑
senses.example: A peacock strutted across the garden path.
senses.exampleCN: 一只孔雀昂首阔步地走过了花园小径。
senses.why: The oldest and central sense is simply the bird: the compound names it by its dark green-blue colour and the crow-like call of the male.
senses.whyCN: 最古老、最核心的义项就是这种鸟本身：这个词的构成正是用蓝黑绿的色彩加上雄鸟似鸦的叫声来命名它。

senses.title: The spread of the train
senses.definition: the display in which the bird fans out its long tail feathers in a shimmering wall of eyespots
senses.definitionCN: 孔雀将长长的尾羽呈扇形展开、形成一面闪烁眼斑墙的展示动作
senses.example: The peacock opened its tail in a wide fan.
senses.exampleCN: 孔雀把尾展开成一把大扇子。
senses.why: Because the train is the bird most striking feature, the noun also names the display itself when the feathers are fully fanned out.
senses.whyCN: 尾屏是这种鸟最醒目的特征，所以名词也从鸟本身转移到「羽毛完全展开的那一面屏」这个动作和画面。

senses.title: A person who shows off
senses.definition: a person who behaves proudly and likes to display their looks, wealth, or achievements
senses.definitionCN: 举止骄傲、喜欢展示自己外表、财富或成就的人
senses.example: He is a bit of a peacock at parties.
senses.exampleCN: 他在聚会上有点爱炫耀。
senses.why: The strutting walk and flaring train became a ready metaphor: anyone who puts on a show of finery is called by the bird name.
senses.whyCN: 孔雀昂首阔步的步伐和张开的尾屏很容易被借来做比喻：谁把华丽外表展示给人看，就会被用这个鸟名来称呼。

senses.title: To strut and show off
senses.definition: to behave proudly, moving about in order to attract attention
senses.definitionCN: 举止骄傲地四处走动以吸引注意
senses.example: The new captain peacocked about the deck in full uniform.
senses.exampleCN: 新船长穿着全套制服在甲板上招摇地走来走去。
senses.why: English often turns an animal noun into a verb, and the peacock supplies the action picture: walking about like a bird on display.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把动物名词直接用作动词，而孔雀提供了现成的动作画面——像一只被展示的鸟那样走来走去。

senses.title: A peacock-blue colour
senses.definition: a rich dark blue-green colour, used of fabric and paint
senses.definitionCN: 一种浓艳的深蓝绿色，常用于布料和涂料
senses.example: The sofa was covered in peacock blue velvet.
senses.exampleCN: 沙发包着孔雀蓝的天鹅绒。
senses.why: The iridescent neck feathers supply a colour term, so the bird name passes into design vocabulary as an adjective.
senses.whyCN: 孔雀颈部羽毛的虹彩给出了一个色号，于是鸟名以形容词的身份进入了设计语汇。

senses.title: Showing off in the animal world
senses.definition: in biology, a costly visual display that an animal uses to attract mates
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中动物为吸引配偶而付出较高代价的视觉展示
senses.example: The male peacock display is a classic example of sexual selection.
senses.exampleCN: 雄孔雀的展示是性选择的经典例子。
senses.why: Research on the bird turned its train into a textbook case, so the word also labels a general pattern of costly display.
senses.whyCN: 对孔雀的研究让它的尾屏成了教科书案例，于是这个词也用来指称「代价高昂的展示」这一普遍模式。

senses.title: A brilliant but showy figure
senses.definition: someone or something that impresses by extravagant looks rather than by solid substance
senses.definitionCN: 靠过于华丽的外表而不是实在内涵来打动人的形象
senses.example: Critics called the scheme a peacock that hid a simple truth.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者称这个方案是一只孔雀，用来遮掩一个简单的真相。
senses.why: When the focus moves from the person to the impression produced, the word becomes a judged image: external brilliance over inner worth.
senses.whyCN: 当焦点从那人本身转移到它给人的印象上，这个词就成了一种带评价的形象：外在光亮压过了内在价值。

intro.en: Peacock is a compound of Old English pea, meaning peafowl, and coc, meaning cock, replacing the earlier name pawa.
intro.cn: peacock 由古英语 pea（孔雀类）与 coc（公鸡）复合而成，取代了更早的名称 pawa。

items.en: Greek taos names the bird after peacock kept for display and thought to be imported from the East.
items.cn: 希腊语 taos 指这种鸟，它在希腊多作观赏饲养，一般认为来自东方。

items.en: Latin pavo names the peacock, probably borrowed from the Greek word.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pavo 指孔雀，一般认为借自希腊语。

items.en: Old English pawa comes into the language from Latin pavo and names the bird early on.
items.cn: 古英语 pawa 由拉丁语 pavo 进入英语，很早就用来指称这种鸟。

items.en: A second name, pea, meaning a peafowl, appears and pairs with coc, the ordinary word for a cock.
items.cn: 表示孔雀类禽鸟的第二个词 pea 出现，并与表示公鸡的常用词 coc 组合。

items.en: The compound pecock is recorded, built from pea plus cock and replacing the older pawa.
items.cn: 复合词 pecock 有记载，由 pea 加 cock 构成，取代了较早的 pawa。

items.en: The spelling settles as peacock, and from the bird the word extends to showy people and to a deep blue-green colour.
items.cn: 拼写稳定为 peacock，并从鸟本身扩展到爱炫耀的人和孔雀蓝色。

note.en: Peacock belongs to a small family of compound bird names, and it is also close to everyday words for vanity and display.
note.cn: peacock 属于一小组复合鸟名词，同时也与表示虚荣和炫耀的日常词相邻。

entries.definition: the female of the peafowl, smaller and duller than the male
entries.definitionCN: 雌孔雀，体型比雄性小、色彩暗淡，是 peacock 的对应雌性名称

entries.definition: a young peafowl
entries.definitionCN: 幼孔雀；共享 pea 词根并接 chick（雏鸟）

entries.definition: the general name for the peacock and peahen together
entries.definitionCN: 孔雀的统称，同时涵盖雌雄两性

entries.definition: a person who tries to attract attention by displaying their abilities
entries.definitionCN: 爱炫耀的人；与 peacock 作人物义时义场最近

entries.definition: a man who pays great attention to his elegant clothes
entries.definitionCN: 衣着考究的男士，往日也带炫耀意味

entries.definition: attractive in a cheap and showy way
entries.definitionCN: 华而不实的；对应孔雀的「格外显眼」意象

normalIntro.en: Peacock works as a picture word: pea for the bird family, cock for the male, and a fanned wall of eyespots for the show.
normalIntro.cn: peacock 很适合当作图画词来记：pea 指孔雀类，cock 表示雄性，再配上展开的满眼斑尾屏这一画面。

normal.en: Pea plus cock: pea names the peafowl and cock marks it as the male.
normal.cn: pea 加 cock：pea 指孔雀类禽鸟，cock 标明它是雄性。

normal.en: The female is a peahen and the young one a peachick, all sharing the pea stem.
normal.cn: 雌性是 peahen，幼鸟是 peachick，都共享 pea 这个词干。

normal.en: Peacock blue is a fixed colour phrase for a rich dark blue-green.
normal.cn: peacock blue 是固定说法，指浓艳的深蓝绿色。

normal.en: The display is verbed as peacocking, meaning strutting to be noticed.
normal.cn: 它的展示动作可以动词化为 peacocking，意为招摇引人注意。

normal.en: Compare pheasant: both are long-tailed game birds in the same pheasant family.
normal.cn: 对比 pheasant：两者都是尾羽长的雉类猎禽，同属雉科。

abstract.en: Picture a wall of hundreds of blue eyes all opening at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一整面墙上数百只蓝色眼睛同时张开。

abstract.en: Picture the moment the fan snaps open and the crowd gasps.
abstract.cn: 想象折扇猛然打开、人群齐声惊叹的那一瞬。

abstract.en: Picture a guest walking into a party all in peacock blue.
abstract.cn: 想象一位客人穿着一身孔雀蓝走进宴会厅。

examples.en: Male peacocks open their tails to attract a mate.
examples.cn: 雄孔雀展开尾屏来吸引配偶。

examples.en: She wore a peacock blue dress to the reception.
examples.cn: 她穿了一条孔雀蓝色的裙子去参加招待会。

examples.en: The director peacocks whenever journalists are in the room.
examples.cn: 只要有记者在场，这位导演就会大出风头。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮可可」——皮上满是可可色的眼斑，一开屏就让人记住；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 pea（孔雀类禽鸟）+ coc（公鸡）构成 peacock；pea 可追溯到拉丁语 pavo（孔雀），一般认为源于希腊语 taos，更早的英语名称是 pawa。

sensesIntro.en: Peacock starts with the bird, grows into its display and its colour, and then flows into metaphor for a showy person, action, or image.
sensesIntro.cn: peacock 从这种鸟本身出发，长出「开屏」和颜色义，再流向比喻：爱炫耀的人、招摇的动作和华丽空洞的形象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fan of blue feathers opening into a wall of eyespots.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面蓝羽折扇展开成布满眼斑的墙。

branches.en: The living bird is the source sense named by the compound.
branches.cn: 活的禽鸟本身是这个词复合命名的源头义项。

branches.en: The fanned train names the display rather than the bird.
branches.cn: 展开的尾屏把焦点从鸟转到「展示」这一动作。

branches.en: The strutting show becomes a person, then a verb for the same action.
branches.cn: 昂首展示先变指一类人，再变成表示同一动作的动词。

branches.en: The neck colour alone supplies a design word.
branches.cn: 单靠颈部羽毛的颜色就形成了一个设计用词。

branches.en: Biology and criticism both read the train as costly display.
branches.cn: 生物学与评论都用孔雀理解「代价高昂的炫耀」。

intro.en: Peacock is a true compound, so its parts are whole English nouns rather than affixes: pea for the peafowl and cock for the male bird.
intro.cn: peacock 是真正的复合词，组成部分都是完整的英语名词而不是词缀：pea 指孔雀类禽鸟，cock 指雄性鸟。

latinIntro.en: Latin pavo is the ancestor of the older English name pawa, while the pea element survives in the family words peahen and peafowl.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pavo 是更早的英语名 pawa 的来源，而 pea 这一部分保留在 peahen 与 peafowl 等同族词中。

items.structure: Old English noun, here a bird name
items.meaningCN: 孔雀类禽鸟（与表示豆子的 pea 不是同一来源）
items.example: The first part of peacock is this bird word.
items.exampleCN: peacock 的前半部分是这个词。

items.example: Cock marks the bird as the male of its kind.
items.exampleCN: cock 标明它是这一类中的雄性。

items.meaning: the blue-green male with a huge train
items.meaningCN: 尾羽华丽的蓝绿色雄鸟
items.example: Peacock is the full compound name.
items.exampleCN: peacock 是完整的复合名。

items.structure: English noun used as a combining form
items.example: The combining form -hen gives the word peahen.
items.exampleCN: 这一构词成分构出 peahen。

items.example: Peahen names the female counterpart.
items.exampleCN: peahen 指雌性孔雀。

items.example: Peafowl covers both sexes.
items.exampleCN: peafowl 涵盖雌雄两性。

items.example: Peachick is built with the chick element.
items.exampleCN: peachick 由 chick 这一构词成分构成。

items.meaning: a shade named after a colour
items.meaningCN: 以某物颜色命名的色号
items.example: The colour phrase peacock blue uses this pattern.
items.exampleCN: 孔雀蓝这一说法就用的是这个模式。

items.example: Peacock blue names the iridescent neck colour.
items.exampleCN: peacock blue 指颈部羽毛的虹彩颜色。

items.example: The suffix -ish gives peacockish.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ish 构成 peacockish。

latinEntries.example: Pavo is the Latin bird name.
latinEntries.exampleCN: pavo 是拉丁语的孔雀名。

definition_zh: 花生；花生米；（复数）很少的钱；微不足道的
definition_en: a small nutlike seed that grows underground in a papery shell, or a very small amount of money
core_image: 一株矮豆藤把果针钻进土里，土下结出两粒鼓鼓的果仁
scene: 田地收完后，孩子们跟着大人把花生连根拔起来，抖掉泥土，露出一串壳。When the field was cleared, children followed the adults pulling peanut plants by the roots, shaking off the soil to show the chains of pods.
sceneCN: 这里 peanut 是「花生」（第 1 个义项：在土里结荚的油料作物）；句意：田收完后，孩子们跟着大人把花生连根拔起，抖掉泥土，露出一串串果荚。

pos.zh: 花生；花生米；（复数）很少的钱

derivatives.zh: 有花生味的；带花生意趣的，由 peanut 加形容词后缀 -y 构成
花生米大小的，意即很小的；由 peanut 加 -sized（……大小的）构成

senses.title: The podded seed that ripens underground
senses.definition: a small edible seed that develops in a papery pod beneath the soil
senses.definitionCN: 在土里的纸质荚壳中发育成熟的小型可食用种子
senses.example: She shelled a handful of peanuts for the birds.
senses.exampleCN: 她剥了一把花生喂鸟。
senses.why: The plant was named for its odd habit: a pea-like plant whose pods ripen like a nut below ground, so the compound joins the two words.
senses.whyCN: 这种植物得名于它奇特的习性：像豌豆却把荚果结在土里，于是这个词把「豆」和「坚果」两个名称合在一起。

senses.title: The plant that flowers above and fruits below
senses.definition: the low-growing plant itself, with yellow flowers whose stalks push the pods down into the soil
senses.definitionCN: 这种矮生植株本身，开黄花，花谢后果针把荚果推进土里
senses.example: They rotate peanut with corn to keep the soil healthy.
senses.exampleCN: 他们让花生和玉米轮作，以保持土壤健康。
senses.why: Because the fruit and the whole plant are named by the same word, the noun shifts from seed to crop depending on context.
senses.whyCN: 果实和整株植物共用一个词，所以这个词在具体语境中会从「种子」滑向「一种作物」。

senses.title: A very small amount of money
senses.titleCN: 很少的钱；微不足道的数目
senses.definition: an amount too small to matter, used almost always in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 小到无所谓的金额，几乎总用复数形式
senses.example: He gets paid peanuts and works all night.
senses.exampleCN: 他挣的钱少得可怜，还要通宵干活。
senses.why: Peanuts are tiny and cheap in the shell, so their small size becomes a unit for small money.
senses.whyCN: 花生米又小又便宜，于是它的小尺寸就被拿来当作「一点点钱」的计量单位。

senses.title: Something trivial in size or importance
senses.definition: anything regarded as too small or too minor to worry about
senses.definitionCN: 任何被认为太小或太次要、不值得在意的事物
senses.example: Compared with the main budget, this is peanuts.
senses.exampleCN: 与主要预算相比，这点钱微不足道。
senses.why: From money the word drifts to any scale comparison: a peanut-sized item is a trivial one.
senses.whyCN: 从钱出发，这个词又漂移到任何程度比较上：花生米大小的事物就是微不足道的事物。

senses.title: The roasted snack and its products
senses.definition: the roasted or salted form eaten as a snack, and products such as butter made from it
senses.definitionCN: 烤制或盐焗后作为零食食用花生粒，以及用它制成的花生酱等产品
senses.example: The bar serves beer and bowls of warm peanuts.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒吧供应啤酒和一碗碗热花生。
senses.why: Once the seed became a mass-market snack, the word moved from the crop to prepared food on the table.
senses.whyCN: 这种种子成为大众零食之后，词义就从田间作物转移到餐桌上的加工食品。

senses.title: A tall, thin, protruding character
senses.definition: in comics, a head and face drawn as a simple rounded shape on a thin line body
senses.definitionCN: 漫画中把头脸画成简单圆润形状、接在细线上身体的画法
senses.example: The cartoonist drew peanuted heroes with no real noses.
senses.exampleCN: 那位漫画家画的花生头主角几乎没有鼻子。
senses.why: The two-lobed shell looks like a tiny head, so illustrators borrowed its shape for round-headed characters.
senses.whyCN: 两瓣的荚壳看上去像一个小脑袋，插画师便借这个形状来画圆头人物。

senses.title: A public gallery seat for people to look down at
senses.definition: in some older English use, the highest and cheapest seats, where the audience looked down on the show
senses.definitionCN: 某些较早期的英语用法中指最高、最便宜的座位，观众可俯视舞台
senses.example: The gallery was nicknamed the peanut gallery after the cheap snack sold there.
senses.exampleCN: 这层楼座因为在那里卖廉价花生而得了「花生席」的绰号。
senses.why: Cheap seats were also where cheap snacks were sold, so the food name was attached to the crowd up there and later to any noisy audience.
senses.whyCN: 便宜座位也是廉价零食出售的地方，于是食品名被安到楼上观众身上，后来更泛指爱起哄的观众。

intro.en: Peanut is a plain English compound of pea and nut, first recorded in the eighteenth century for a plant whose seed ripened underground.
intro.cn: peanut 是英语里直接由 pea 与 nut 复合而成的词，十八世纪开始有记载，用来指果实结在土里的那种植物。

items.en: Pea and nut are both old English words for familiar food, pea through Latin pisum from Greek pison.
items.cn: pea 与 nut 都是表示常见食物的古英语词，其中 pea 经由拉丁语 pisum 来自希腊语 pison。

items.en: Spanish explorers in the Americas meet the plant and call its seeds cacahuete, from Nahuatl, while European settlers take the crop to Africa and Asia.
items.cn: 西班牙探险者在美洲见到这种植物，称其种子为 cacahuete（源自纳瓦特尔语），欧洲移民又把这种作物带到非洲和亚洲。

items.en: Writers describe the plant as a pea that fruits underground, and the compound name peanut appears for the seed.
items.cn: 作者们把这种植物描述为「在土里结果的豌豆」，描述其种子的复合词 peanut 出现。

items.en: Groundnut is the earlier commercial American name, and peanut settles as the everyday word in British and American English.
items.cn: groundnut 是更早的商业名称，peanut 随后在英式与美式英语中都稳定为日常用词。

items.en: Peanuts as a cheap snack leads to the money phrase work for peanuts and to the peanut gallery of cheap seats.
items.cn: 花生作为廉价零食这一事实带出了「为微薄报酬干活」的说法，以及指廉价楼座的花生席。

items.en: Peanut butter turns the crop into a staple, and peanut joins scientific and medical compounds such as peanut allergy.
items.cn: 花生酱把它变成主食级商品，peanut 又进入花生过敏等科学与医学复合说法。

note.en: Peanut is a food compound, its nearest relatives are other pod and oil-seed names, and its figurative sense is close to every word for small money.
note.cn: peanut 是食物类复合词，最近的同族是其他荚果与油料名，而其比喻义与所有表示小额钱的词相邻。

entries.definition: the older English name for the peanut, from its growing underground
entries.definitionCN: 花生的较早英语名称，得名于果实结在土里；与 peanut 同指一物

entries.definition: a large brown nut from a tree, not a podded seed
entries.definitionCN: 树上的大颗褐色坚果；与 peanut 同样以 nut 结尾，但词源不同

entries.definition: a hard-shelled wrinkled nut, from Old English wealh, foreign
entries.definitionCN: 外壳坚硬、果仁有皱纹的坚果，来自古英语外来成分 wealh

entries.definition: the small round nut of the hazel tree
entries.definitionCN: 榛树的小圆坚果；同属以 nut 结尾的食物复合词

entries.definition: a soft spread made from milk, and the base for peanut butter
entries.definitionCN: 由牛奶制成的软抹酱，是花生酱这一搭配的另一半

entries.definition: a plant of the pea family that ripens its seeds in pods
entries.definitionCN: 豆科植物，种子在荚中成熟；花生在植物学上属于豆科

entries.definition: a very small amount of money given as payment
entries.definitionCN: 微薄的报酬；与表示小额钱的花生义最接近

normalIntro.en: Peanut is built from two ordinary food words, pea and nut, and its naming picture is a pod that ripens under the ground.
normalIntro.cn: peanut 由 pea 和 nut 两个普通食物词构成，命名画面是「荚果结在土里」。

normal.en: Pea plus nut: a plant like a pea whose seeds are eaten like nuts.
normal.cn: pea 加 nut：像豌豆一样的植物，种子却像坚果那样吃。

normal.en: The older name groundnut says the same thing from the ground up.
normal.cn: 较早的名称 groundnut 从「地下」的角度表达了同一个意思。

normal.en: Peanut butter shows the seed as a spread rather than a nut.
normal.cn: peanut butter 表明这种种子更常被当作抹酱而不是坚果。

normal.en: Work for peanuts uses the seed small size for small pay.
normal.cn: 「为微薄报酬干活」这一说法借用了花生米的小尺寸来表示小额报酬。

normal.en: Compare walnut and chestnut: same nut element, different origin words.
normal.cn: 对比 walnut 与 chestnut：nut 这一成分相同，前半部分来源不同。

abstract.en: Picture a yellow flower curving down and pushing its pod into the soil.
abstract.cn: 想象一朵黄花向下弯曲，把结出的荚推进土里。

abstract.en: Picture a thin plant pulled up with a chain of pods hanging like beads.
abstract.cn: 想象拔起一株细矮的植物，上面挂着一串像珠子一样的荚。

abstract.en: Picture a coin purse emptied out and only shells left.
abstract.cn: 想象把零钱包倒空，只剩下几片壳。

examples.en: Peanut allergy can be severe in young children.
examples.cn: 小孩子的花生过敏可能很严重。

examples.en: He was paid peanuts for three months of work.
examples.cn: 干了三个月，他只拿到微薄的报酬。

examples.en: Farmers rotate peanuts with cereals to add nitrogen to the soil.
examples.cn: 农民让花生与谷类轮作，为土壤补充氮。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮花生」——剥掉那层纸一样的「皮」，才见到两粒花生米；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 pea（豌豆，源自拉丁语 pisum、希腊语 pison）+ nut（坚果）构成 peanut；这个词是一八世纪起英语自行构拟的描述性复合名，不是拉丁词根派生，同义词 groundnut 从「地下」的角度命名同一植物。

sensesIntro.en: Peanut names the seed, then the crop, then a snack, and from its small cheap size it spreads to small money, minor matters, and even seats and cartoon heads.
sensesIntro.cn: peanut 先指种子，再指作物、零食，又因「小而便宜」扩展到小额钱、鸡毛蒜皮之事，甚至楼座和漫画头像。
