definition_zh: 啄；轻吻；匆匆吃几口；（复数）轻吻
definition_en: to strike or bite something with a sharp beak, or to give a quick light kiss
core_image: 鸟喙向下一探，像钉子一样在目标上一点就起
scene: 清晨的湖边，一只白鹭低头探进浅水，用细长的喙飞快地戳起一条小鱼。At dawn by the lake, the heron dipped its head and pecked a small fish out of the shallows.
sceneCN: 这里 peck 是「用喙啄」（第 1 个义项：鸟用喙戳啄东西）；句意：清晨的湖边，一只白鹭低头探进浅水，用细长的喙飞快地戳起一条小鱼。

collocations.zh: 把饭挑来挑去不肯好好吃
一点一点地啄；一点一点地啃
强弱次序（原指家鸡的啄序）

derivatives.zh: 由词根加 -er 构成，指「啄食的鸟」或「啄木鸟」
由 peck 加 -ish 构成，义为「有点饿的」，英国口语常用
wood（木头）+ pecker（啄木的鸟），指「啄木鸟」
pecking（啄）+ order（次序），由家鸡互啄现象而来，指「等级次序」

senses.title: To bite with a beak
senses.definition: to strike or pick at something with the beak, especially food
senses.definitionCN: 用喙戳、啄或拾取东西，尤指食物
senses.example: Sparrows pecked crumbs from the table.
senses.exampleCN: 麻雀啄走了桌上的面包屑。
senses.why: The core image is one sharp downward point of a beak, and from it comes the plain action of birds feeding.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是鸟喙向下猛地一点，由这个动作直接长出「鸟啄食」这个最基本的义项。

senses.title: To kiss lightly
senses.definition: to kiss someone quickly and lightly, as a bird might touch with its beak
senses.definitionCN: 像鸟用喙轻点一样，快速地亲吻某人
senses.example: He pecked her on the cheek and ran to the car.
senses.exampleCN: 他在她脸颊上轻吻一下就奔向汽车。
senses.why: A quick touch-and-lift is all a peck is, so the bird action extends to a fast, light kiss.
senses.whyCN: 「啄」本身就是一碰即离，于是从鸟的动作自然延伸出又快又轻的亲吻。

senses.title: To eat only tiny amounts
senses.definition: to pick at food and eat it in very small amounts
senses.definitionCN: 把食物挑来挑去，只吃一点点
senses.example: The child pecked at her dinner without appetite.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子没胃口，把晚饭挑来挑去没怎么吃。
senses.why: Birds eat one grain at a time, so a person who eats like that picks and eats in tiny bites.
senses.whyCN: 鸟是一粒一粒进食的，人作出同样的吃法时，就指挑挑拣拣、只吃两三口。

senses.title: A small bird unit of measure
senses.titleCN: 啄食量（鸟类饲养的计量单位）
senses.definition: a historical unit of measure for the feed or grain given to birds
senses.definitionCN: 旧时给鸟类饲料或谷物计量的单位
senses.example: The old feed book lists a peck of grain for each bird.
senses.exampleCN: 旧饲料账簿上给每只鸟记一小啄谷料。
senses.why: Since one peck is one bite, the word was once used for a small measured amount of feed.
senses.whyCN: 一啄就是一口的量，所以这个词曾被用作少量饲料的计量说法。

senses.title: To nag or find fault
senses.definition: to keep finding fault with someone with repeated small criticisms
senses.definitionCN: 一次又一次挑出别人的小毛病
senses.example: She pecked at every detail in the report.
senses.exampleCN: 她对报告里每一个细节都不停挑刺。
senses.why: Small repeated jabs from a beak turn into small repeated words aimed at someone.
senses.whyCN: 一遍遍的小啄，引申为一句句落在别人身上的小批评，就是不停挑刺数落。

senses.title: A quick kiss
senses.definition: a brief, light kiss
senses.definitionCN: 短暂而轻的一下亲吻
senses.example: She gave her son a peck before his exam.
senses.exampleCN: 儿子考试前，她轻轻吻了他一下。
senses.why: The noun names the event itself, one quick contact, just as one peck is one hit.
senses.whyCN: 名词直接指这一次动作，正如一下啄是一击，一次轻吻也只是一碰。

senses.title: In the phrase peck and perch
senses.definition: in informal speech, food and a place to sleep or live
senses.definitionCN: 口语中把吃食与栖身之所合称
senses.example: New workers look for peck and perch in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 新来的工人到城里寻一个吃住的地方。
senses.why: Birds peck for food and perch on a branch to rest, so the pair names the two basic needs.
senses.whyCN: 鸟啄食求饱、落枝求歇，于是「啄」与「栖」合起来表示吃和住两件基本需求。

senses.title: Pecking order
senses.definition: the social rank among animals or people, shown by who may peck whom
senses.definitionCN: 动物或人之间的社会等级，由谁可以啄谁体现
senses.example: Every team has its own pecking order.
senses.exampleCN: 每个团队都有自己的等级次序。
senses.why: Hens in a flock peck only those below them, so the peck itself draws the ladder of rank.
senses.whyCN: 鸡群里的鸡只啄比它地位低的同伴，于是「啄」这个动作直接画出了等级阶梯。

intro.en: Peck was first a noun for a bird unit of measure and then became a verb, and its exact root is not settled.
intro.cn: peck 先作名词表示鸟的计量单位，后变为动词，确切词根尚无定论。

items.en: The word has no secure root; some link it to pick, but that is only one hypothesis.
items.cn: 该词没有可靠的词根来源，有人把它与 pick 联系，但这只是一种假说。

items.en: Peck appears as a noun for a unit of dry measure used for feed.
items.cn: 中古英语中 peck 先指干量单位，用于计量饲料。

items.en: The verb pecken means to strike with the beak.
items.cn: 英语 pecken 作动词，意为用喙戳啄。

items.en: The noun also names the action of a beak, one quick point.
items.cn: 名词也用来指鸟喙的一下动作，即快速的一戳。

items.en: Figurative uses grow for light kisses and for eating in small amounts.
items.cn: 引申用法出现，既指轻吻，也指小口小口地吃。

items.en: Pecking order becomes a general term for social rank.
items.cn: 美式英语中 pecking order 成为表示社会等级的通用说法。

note.en: Peck is the quick beak stroke, beside the words for picking, nipping, and eating little by little.
note.cn: peck 指鸟喙快速一点，与「拾取、轻咬、小口吃」一类的词相邻。

entries.definition: to choose, or to gather something with the fingers or beak
entries.definitionCN: 挑选；用手指或喙拾取（只是拼写与读音相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a bird that pecks, or a woodpecker
slightly hungry
a bird that pecks holes in trees
to take small repeated bites
to give a sharp small bite
to feed on grass slowly

normalIntro.en: A peck is one sharp point of a beak that strikes and lifts at once, and its best memory hooks are peck at, a peck on the cheek, and pecking order.
normalIntro.cn: peck 是鸟喙一下子点到又抬起，记忆抓手是「点着吃」「轻轻一吻」与「啄序」三种用法。

normal.en: Peck at means to eat in small bites, like a hen at the grain.
normal.cn: peck at 表示小口地吃，就像母鸡啄米。

normal.en: A peck on the cheek is a quick and light kiss.
normal.cn: a peck on the cheek 是飞快而轻的一下亲吻。

normal.en: In a pecking order, higher birds peck lower ones.
normal.cn: 在啄序中，地位高的鸟去啄地位低的鸟。

normal.en: Woodpecker joins wood and pecker, a bird that pecks wood.
normal.cn: woodpecker 由 wood 与 pecker 合成，就是啄木头的鸟。

normal.en: Peckish, from peck, means slightly hungry and ready to peck at food.
normal.cn: peckish 由 peck 变来，意思是有点饿、想啄点东西吃。

abstract.en: Think of a sparrow tapping a crumb three times a second.
abstract.cn: 想象一只麻雀一秒三下地啄面包屑。

abstract.en: Picture a kiss as brief as a beak touching a cheek.
abstract.cn: 把轻吻想成鸟喙轻触脸颊那样一碰就离。

abstract.en: See a hungry child pushing dinner around like a bird at grain.
abstract.cn: 想象一个没胃口的孩子把晚饭推来推去，像鸟拨弄谷粒。

examples.en: The pigeon pecked at the bread on the pavement.
examples.cn: 鸽子啄食人行道上的面包。

examples.en: She gave him a quick peck on the cheek.
examples.cn: 她在他的脸颊上轻轻一吻。

examples.en: Every office has its own pecking order.
examples.cn: 每个办公室都有自己的等级次序。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派克」钢笔尖向纸面一点一抬，正像鸟喙啄食；只作画面联想，与词源无关。

root: 词根来源不确定（一般认为与 pick 同源，但未有定论）：中古英语 peck 作为干量计量单位出现，后引申为「用喙啄」的动作，核心义是「喙的一点」。

sensesIntro.en: Peck starts as a bird striking food with its beak, spreads to a quick light kiss and to eating in tiny amounts, and levels out in the phrases pecking order and peck and perch.
sensesIntro.cn: peck 起于鸟用喙戳食物，先引申为又快又轻的亲吻与小口挑食，再稳定在「啄序」和「吃住」这类固定说法里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a beak that shoots down, taps the target, and lifts at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：鸟喙向下一点，点到目标立刻抬起。

branches.en: The bird action itself is the base sense.
branches.cn: 鸟用喙啄食本身是最基础的义项。

branches.en: The quick touch becomes both the act and the event of a light kiss.
branches.cn: 「一碰即离」既演成轻吻的动作，也演成这一次轻吻本身。

branches.en: Small repeated pecks become tiny bites and small nagging criticisms.
branches.cn: 一次次小啄，既指小口进食，也指一句句挑刺。

branches.en: A peck as one bite survives in measures of feed and in the phrase for food and lodging.
branches.cn: 「一口之量」留在饲料计量与「吃住」的说法里。

branches.en: Who may peck whom draws the rank ladder of a flock.
branches.cn: 谁可以啄谁，画出了鸟群中的等级阶梯。

intro.en: Peck is a short native English word with no Latin stem, but several English words grow from it.
intro.cn: peck 是简短的英语本土词，没有拉丁词干，但由它长出了好几个英语词。

latinIntro.en: Peck has no Latin ancestor, and the classical word for pecking, mordere, is unrelated.
latinIntro.cn: peck 没有拉丁语祖先，古典拉丁语里表示「啄」的 mordere 与它并无亲缘关系。

items.example: Peck is the base verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: peck 是这个词族的基础动词。

items.meaning: a light kiss or a beak stroke
items.example: The noun keeps the quick touch.
items.exampleCN: 名词保留了「快速一碰」的意思。

items.example: The suffix -er turns peck into pecker.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 把 peck 变成 pecker。

items.example: Pecker names the bird that pecks.
items.exampleCN: pecker 指啄食的鸟。

items.example: The suffix -ish forms peckish.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ish 构成 peckish。

items.example: Peckish describes mild hunger.
items.exampleCN: peckish 描述轻微的饥饿感。

items.example: Wood combines with pecker in woodpecker.
items.exampleCN: wood 与 pecker 合成 woodpecker。

items.meaning: a bird that pecks holes in trees
items.example: Woodpecker is a two-part compound noun.
items.exampleCN: woodpecker 是两部分合成的名词。

items.example: The suffix -ing gives pecking in pecking order.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 在 pecking order 中给出 pecking。

items.example: Order joins pecking to name social rank.
items.exampleCN: order 与 pecking 连用表示社会等级。

definition_zh: 脚蹬；踏板；踩踏板；（钢琴）延音踏板
definition_en: a lever worked by the foot to control a machine, vehicle, or musical instrument, or to work such a lever
core_image: 脚底下一块可以踩下去的横杆，一压一松，力量就传给了轮子
scene: 上坡前，骑行者把脚踩稳，用脚尖努力向下一推。On the steep hill, the cyclist pressed down hard on the pedal with the ball of her foot.
sceneCN: 这里 pedal 是「脚踏板」（第 1 个义项：自行车等上面用脚踩的装置）；句意：上坡时，骑行者用脚掌前部用力向下踩脚踏板。

pos.zh: 脚踏板；踏板；（钢琴的）踏板
脚的；足部的（用于 pedal 开头的医学与解剖用语）

collocations.zh: 柔音踏板；弱化（某种说法）
把油门踩到底；全力加速

derivatives.zh: 由 pedal 加 -er 构成，指「骑车的人」，美式写作 pedaler
由 pedal 缩短加 -o 构成，指「脚踏船」，英国英语常用
由 pedal 加 -ing 构成，指「踩踏板的动作」，美式拼写

senses.title: The foot lever itself
senses.definition: a lever on a machine or vehicle that is pushed with the foot
senses.definitionCN: 机器或车辆上用脚推动的杠杆
senses.example: The bike pedals were worn smooth.
senses.exampleCN: 自行车的脚踏板被磨得光溜溜的。
senses.why: The core image is a foot lever, and naming the object is the most direct sense.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象就是脚下那块可以踩的横杆，直接指这个东西是最近的义项。

senses.title: To work the pedals
senses.definition: to move the pedals of a bicycle or other machine with the feet
senses.definitionCN: 用脚推动自行车或其他机器的踏板
senses.example: He pedalled slowly up the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 他慢慢地蹬车上坡。
senses.why: From the object, the word shifts to the action of pressing it, so pedal becomes a verb.
senses.whyCN: 从「踏板」这个物件转到「踩踏板」的动作，pedal 于是从名词变成动词。

senses.title: The car foot controls
senses.definition: the accelerator or brake control worked by the foot in a vehicle
senses.definitionCN: 汽车上用脚控制的油门或刹车装置
senses.example: She hit the brake pedal just in time.
senses.exampleCN: 她及时踩下了刹车踏板。
senses.why: Any machine that turns foot pressure into control calls its lever a pedal, and cars are the common case.
senses.whyCN: 凡是用脚压出控制的机器，其杠杆都叫踏板，汽车是最常见的场合。

senses.title: The piano sustain control
senses.definition: the foot lever on a piano, especially the right one, that keeps notes sounding
senses.definitionCN: 钢琴上尤其是右侧的脚控装置，能让音延续不断
senses.example: Hold the pedal while the chord rings.
senses.exampleCN: 和弦响着的时候踩着延音踏板别松。
senses.why: In music the same foot lever controls sound rather than motion, but the object is still a pedal.
senses.whyCN: 在音乐里同一块脚控装置控制的是声音而不是运动，但物件仍是同一类踏板。

senses.title: The organ foot keyboard
senses.definition: a set of keys played with the feet on a pipe organ
senses.definitionCN: 管风琴上用脚弹奏的一组键
senses.example: His foot found the pedal and the bass note boomed.
senses.exampleCN: 他的脚找到了脚踏键，低音轰然响起。
senses.why: A row of foot keys is a pedal board, so the word pulls in the feet-played register of the organ.
senses.whyCN: 一排用脚弹的键叫脚踏板组，于是这个词也指管风琴上用脚演奏的那一部分。

senses.title: To ride by turning pedals
senses.definition: to travel on a bicycle or pedalled craft
senses.definitionCN: 骑自行车或脚踏船等出行
senses.example: We pedalled along the river to the market.
senses.exampleCN: 我们沿着河边骑车去市场。
senses.why: Once the verb means to pedal, it can name the whole journey made by pedalling.
senses.whyCN: 动词既然表示踩踏板，也就顺理成章地表示「踩着踏板走完一段路」。

senses.title: To soften or tone down
senses.definition: to make a statement less strong or less noticeable
senses.definitionCN: 把某种说法说得轻一些、不那么醒目
senses.example: The report soft-pedalled the serious risks.
senses.exampleCN: 报道淡化了那些严重的风险。
senses.why: The soft pedal of a piano lowers the sound, so to soft-pedal a claim is to turn its volume down.
senses.whyCN: 钢琴的柔音踏板能把声音压小，所以「软化某个说法」就像把它的音量调低。

senses.title: Barely keeping pace
senses.titleCN: 勉强跟上；（口语）勉强维持
senses.definition: in informal use, to keep something just at the level needed
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示把某事勉强维持在所需水平
senses.example: She kept to the pedal all through the long ride.
senses.exampleCN: 整段长途骑行她始终踩着踏板勉强跟上。
senses.why: A rider who never lifts the foot stays just level with the others, so the phrase carries a sense of strain.
senses.whyCN: 骑车人一直不抬脚，才能勉强与同伴并排，这个说法因此带有吃力的意味。

intro.en: Pedal comes through French from Latin pedalis, of the foot, from pes, a foot, and it first named the foot lever of the organ.
intro.cn: pedal 经法语来自拉丁语 pedalis（脚的），出自 pes（脚），最初指管风琴的脚踏装置。

items.en: Pes, pedis means a foot, and pedalis means relating to the foot.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pes、pedis 意为「脚」，pedalis 意为「与脚有关的」。

items.en: Pedale names the treadle worked by the foot on an organ.
items.cn: 法语 pedale 指管风琴上用脚踩动的踏板。

items.en: Pedal enters English as the foot lever of the organ and of the harp.
items.cn: pedal 进入英语，指管风琴与竖琴的脚踏装置。

items.en: With bicycles and cars, the word spreads to foot levers of machines.
items.cn: 随着自行车与汽车出现，这个词扩展到各种机器的脚踏板。

items.en: The noun becomes a verb, to work the pedals.
items.cn: 名词转作动词，表示踩动踏板。

items.en: Phrases such as soft-pedal and back-pedal carry the word into figurative use.
items.cn: soft-pedal、back-pedal 等说法把这个词带进比喻用法。

note.en: Pedal is the foot-operated lever, next to the derived pedal words and to the general levers of bikes, cars, and pianos.
note.cn: pedal 指用脚操作的杠杆，与它派生的词以及自行车、汽车、钢琴上的各种杠杆相邻。

entries.definition: to sell goods by carrying them from place to place
entries.definitionCN: 沿街叫卖；兜售（与 pedal 读音相同、词源不同）

entries.definition: care and treatment of the feet and toenails
entries.definitionCN: 修脚；足部护理，与 pedal 共享 ped-（脚）词根

entries.definition: the base that supports a statue or column
entries.definitionCN: 雕像或柱子的底座（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a lever pressed by the foot to turn a machine
a brake worked by the foot
entries.definitionCN: 脚刹车；用脚操作的制动器

entries.definition: a bar used to move or control something

normalIntro.en: Pedal is built on the Latin foot, and the memory hooks are the bike, the car, and the piano, where each foot lever does a different job.
normalIntro.cn: pedal 的词根是拉丁语的「脚」，记忆抓手在自行车、汽车和钢琴这三处，各有一块用脚控制的踏板。

normal.en: Latin pes gives the foot in both pedal and pedestrian.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pes 把「脚」义同时带进 pedal 与 pedestrian。

normal.en: A brake pedal is the one you press hardest.
normal.cn: brake pedal 往往是你压得最用力的一块。

normal.en: To soft-pedal a problem is to make it sound smaller than it is.
normal.cn: soft-pedal 一个问题，就是让它听起来比实际小。

normal.en: To back-pedal is to go into reverse on a decision.
normal.cn: back-pedal 就是在决定上往回退。

normal.en: Keep pedal and peddle apart: one is the foot lever, the other is selling goods.
normal.cn: 记住 pedal 与 peddle 的区别：一个是脚踏板，一个是兜售货物。

abstract.en: Picture the steady up and down of a rider on a long hill.
abstract.cn: 想象骑行者在上坡路上不停上下踩踏的画面。

abstract.en: See a driver slamming the brake pedal as a light turns red.
abstract.cn: 想象红灯亮起时司机一脚猛踩刹车踏板。

abstract.en: Think of a chord ringing on while the pedal foot stays down.
abstract.cn: 想象踩着延音踏板的脚不抬，和弦就一直响着。

examples.en: Press the pedal gently so the car does not jerk.
examples.cn: 轻轻踩下踏板，这样车子就不会猛一顿。

examples.en: They pedalled all the way across the city.
examples.cn: 他们一路骑车穿过了整座城市。

examples.en: The pianist lifted her foot from the pedal.
examples.cn: 钢琴家把脚从延音踏板上抬起。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拍得」——脚一下一下「拍得」下去，轮子才转起来；只作读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pes、pedis（脚）→ pedalis（脚的）→ 法语 pedale（管风琴踏板）→ 英语 pedal，核心义「用脚操作的杠杆」。同根词还有 pedestrian、podiatrist 等。

sensesIntro.en: Pedal begins as the object, a foot lever, then moves to the action of pressing it, covers the levers of car, piano, and organ, and finally widens to riding and to figurative phrasing.
sensesIntro.cn: pedal 先从实物「脚踏板」开始，再转为「踩踏板」的动作，扩展出汽车、钢琴、管风琴的踏板，最后延伸到骑车与比喻说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bar under the foot that presses down and springs back.
core.cn: 核心意象：脚下的一块横杆，踩下去、弹回来。

branches.en: The object itself is the base sense.
branches.cn: 「踏板」这个物件本身是最基础的义项。

branches.en: Pressing the lever grows into the action and into the ride made by pedalling.
branches.cn: 踩杠杆的动作为动词义，并延伸成骑车出行的整段行程。

branches.en: Car controls, piano sustain, and organ keys are all foot levers in other settings.
branches.cn: 汽车控制、钢琴延音与管风琴脚踏键，都是其他场合的同一种脚控杠杆。

branches.en: The soft pedal of a piano lends its image to toning down a claim.
branches.cn: 钢琴柔音踏板把「压低声量」的意象借给了「淡化说法」。

branches.en: Riding without lifting the foot suggests strain and staying just level.
branches.cn: 一路不抬脚地骑，暗示吃力与勉强持平。

intro.en: Pedal is built on the Latin foot ped-, with English and French relatives around it.
intro.cn: pedal 筑在拉丁语表示「脚」的词干 ped- 之上，周围还有英语与法语同族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin pes and pedis mean foot, and pedalis means of the foot; the same stem appears in pedestrian, pedestal, and expedite.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pes、pedis 意为脚，pedalis 意为与脚有关；同一词干也见于 pedestrian、pedestal 与 expedite。

items.example: The root ped- appears in pedal and pedestrian.
items.exampleCN: 词根 ped- 见于 pedal 与 pedestrian。

items.example: Pedal keeps the foot meaning.
items.exampleCN: pedal 保留了「脚」的含义。

items.example: Pedal works as a verb too.
items.exampleCN: pedal 也可以作动词。

items.example: The suffix -al forms the Latin adjective pedalis.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成拉丁语形容词 pedalis。

items.example: The suffix -er forms pedaller.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 pedaller。

items.example: Pedaller names the rider.
items.exampleCN: pedaller 指骑车的人。

items.example: Pedalo shortens pedal and adds -o.
items.exampleCN: pedalo 截短 pedal 并加上 -o。

items.example: The suffix -ing gives pedaling.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 pedaling。

items.example: Soft joins pedal in soft-pedal.
items.exampleCN: soft 与 pedal 合成 soft-pedal。

items.example: Back joins pedal in back-pedal.
items.exampleCN: back 与 pedal 合成 back-pedal。

definition_zh: 行人；步行者；平淡乏味的；步行区的
definition_en: a person walking along a road, or dull and uninspired in style or content
core_image: 一个人靠两条腿走在车流之间，慢慢而平常
scene: 晚高峰的人行横道上，一位老人拎着菜篮慢慢走过斑马线，两侧的车都停了下来。At rush hour, an elderly pedestrian crossed the zebra crossing with a shopping basket while the cars waited.
sceneCN: 这里 pedestrian 是「行人」（第 1 个义项：在路上步行的人）；句意：晚高峰时，一位老年行人提着购物篮走过斑马线，车辆都在等候。

pos.zh: 平淡无味的；缺乏想象力的；步行者的

derivatives.zh: 由 pedestrian 加 -ise 构成，义为「把街道改为步行专用」
由 pedestrianise 加 -ed 构成，义为「已改为步行专用的」
由 pedestrian 加 -ism 构成，指「步行运动」或「平淡无奇的风格」
由 pedestrianise 加 -ation 构成，指「街道步行化」

senses.title: A person on foot
senses.definition: a person who is walking, especially along a road
senses.definitionCN: 尤其在路上行走的人
senses.example: The lorry turned without seeing the pedestrian.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车转弯时没有看见那位行人。
senses.why: The Latin base is the foot, and a foot traveller is the plainest sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根就是「脚」，用脚走路的人便是这个词最朴素的意思。

senses.title: Dull and uninspired
senses.titleCN: 平淡乏味的；没有想象力的
senses.definition: ordinary, uninteresting, and lacking imagination in style or content
senses.definitionCN: 普通、无趣，在风格或内容上缺乏想象力
senses.example: His speech was long and pedestrian.
senses.exampleCN: 他的演讲又长又平淡。
senses.why: Walking is slow and plain next to driving, so the word can call writing or talk plodding and flat.
senses.whyCN: 与开车的快速相比，走路缓慢而普通，于是这个词形容文章或讲话时就是「拖沓、平淡」。

senses.title: Relating to walking
senses.definition: designed for or used by people walking rather than by vehicles
senses.definitionCN: 为人步行而非车辆而设计或使用的
senses.example: The city opened a new pedestrian area.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市新开了一个步行区。
senses.why: As a modifier it marks what serves foot travellers, such as a crossing or a zone.
senses.whyCN: 作定语时，它标注那些为人步行服务的设施，比如人行横道或步行区。

senses.title: A passenger who walks
senses.definition: in older use, a traveller who goes a part of the way on foot
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法，指一段路途靠步行完成的旅客
senses.example: The coach dropped the walking travellers at the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 大车在桥边让那些步行旅人下了车。
senses.why: Before cars, a pedestrian could still be a passenger, a person who finished the trip walking.
senses.whyCN: 在汽车普及之前，旅客也可能下车步行一段，于是行人与旅人的身份曾经重叠。

senses.title: The pedestrian as an athlete
senses.definition: in the history of sport, an athlete who competed in walking or running races
senses.definitionCN: 体育史上参加竞走或跑步比赛的运动员
senses.example: The famous pedestrian covered many miles in a week.
senses.exampleCN: 那位著名的步行健将一周走了许多英里。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century sport used pedestrian for any competitor on foot, a now faded sense.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪的体育用 pedestrian 指任何用脚参赛的人，如今这层意思已经很少用。

senses.title: Prose without flair
senses.definition: lacking imagination or elegance, said of prose or style
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏想象或优美感，多用于形容文笔与风格
senses.example: Her first novel was competent but pedestrian.
senses.exampleCN: 她的第一部小说写得还过得去，但平淡无华。
senses.why: The dull sense hardens into a standard critical label for writing and art.
senses.whyCN: 「平淡」这一评价固定下来，成了评论写作与艺术时的标准标签。

senses.title: Unremarkable in an idea or plan
senses.titleCN: （想法、方案）老套的；乏善可陈的
senses.definition: ordinary to the point of being forgettable, said of ideas or plans
senses.definitionCN: 普通到让人记不住，多用于形容想法或方案
senses.example: The proposal is safe and pedestrian.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案稳妥，但乏善可陈。
senses.why: Anything that just walks along without a leap of thought gets called pedestrian.
senses.whyCN: 任何只按部就班、没有思维跳跃的东西，都可以被称为 pedestrian。

senses.title: On foot, in older phrasing
senses.definition: in older style, going on foot rather than riding
senses.definitionCN: 旧式说法，指步行前往而非乘车骑马
senses.example: He made a pedestrian journey to the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 他徒步走去了海边。
senses.why: The plain adverbial use, a journey on foot, survives only in formal or literary wording.
senses.whyCN: 纯粹表示「步行前往」的用法，如今只在正式或文学笔调里才见得到。

intro.en: Pedestrian is built on the Latin pes, pedis, a foot, and has meant a walker for a very long time.
intro.cn: pedestrian 筑在拉丁语 pes、pedis（脚）之上，很早就有「步行者」的意思。

items.en: Pes, pedis means a foot, and pedestris means going on foot.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pes、pedis 意为「脚」，pedestris 意为「步行的」。

items.en: Eques and pedes set apart the horseman and the foot soldier.
items.cn: eques 与 pedes 把骑马与步行的人区分开来，后者即步兵。

items.en: Pedestrian enters English from Latin pedestris, meaning going on foot.
items.cn: pedestrian 由拉丁语 pedestris 进入英语，义为步行。

items.en: The noun names a person who walks, often a traveller on foot.
items.cn: 名词指走路的人，常指徒步的旅人。

items.en: The adjective comes to mean dull and uninspired in writing or talk.
items.cn: 形容词引申出「平淡乏味、缺乏想象力」的评价义。

items.en: Traffic terms such as pedestrians crossing and pedestrian zone spread widely.
items.cn: 现代英语里，「人行横道」「步行区」这类交通用语广泛流行。

note.en: Pedestrian is the walker built on the Latin foot, close to its ped- relatives and to the words for walkers and dull style.
note.cn: pedestrian 是筑在拉丁语「脚」上的步行者，与同根词以及「走路的人」「平淡」一类的词相邻。

entries.definition: a foot lever on a machine or instrument
entries.definitionCN: 脚踏板，与 pedestrian 共享 ped-（脚）词根

entries.definition: the base on which a statue stands
entries.definitionCN: 底座；基座，同样出自「脚」的词根

entries.definition: a doctor who treats problems of the feet
entries.definitionCN: 足病医生（ped- 与 pod- 是同一词根的变体）

entries.definition: a person who is walking by choice
entries.definitionCN: 步行者；常指为了锻炼而走路的人

entries.definition: a person who is going past a place
not interesting or exciting

normalIntro.en: Pedestrian carries the Latin foot, so a pedestrian is a person on foot, and a slow dull style is called pedestrian too.
normalIntro.cn: pedestrian 带着拉丁语的「脚」，所以行人就是靠脚走路的人，而缓慢平淡的文风也被叫作 pedestrian。

normal.en: The root ped- means foot, as in pedal and pedestrian.
normal.cn: 词根 ped- 意为「脚」，pedal 与 pedestrian 都用它。

normal.en: A pedestrian crossing is where the walker has the right of way.
normal.cn: 在人行横道上，行人有优先通过权。

normal.en: A pedestrian street bans vehicles and lets people walk freely.
normal.cn: 步行街禁止车辆驶入，让人们自由行走。

normal.en: Describe a flat, boring book as pedestrian writing.
normal.cn: 形容一本平淡没意思的书，可以说写得 pedestrian。

normal.en: Keep pedestrian and pedicure close: both come back to the foot.
normal.cn: 把 pedestrian 与 pedicure 放在一起记：两者都回到「脚」。

abstract.en: See a slow crowd of walkers crossing while cars wait.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人行慢慢走过，车辆在旁等候。

abstract.en: Think of a dull speech that goes on like a long flat walk.
abstract.cn: 想象一场像漫长平路一样拖下去的乏味演讲。

abstract.en: Picture a city turning a busy road into a street for feet only.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城市把繁忙马路改造成只许步行的街道。

examples.en: Drivers must give way to pedestrians at the crossing.
examples.cn: 司机必须在人行横道处给行人让行。

examples.en: The film is well made but the story is pedestrian.
examples.cn: 这部影片制作精良，但故事平淡。

examples.en: A narrow pedestrian lane runs behind the market.
examples.cn: 市场后面有一条狭窄的步行小道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派德斯特里安」——一「派」行人「得」在马路上慢慢逛；只作读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pes、pedis（脚）→ pedestris（步行的，与 eques 骑马者相对）→ 英语 pedestrian，核心义「用脚走路的人」，再引申为「平淡乏味的」。同根词有 pedestal、expedition。

sensesIntro.en: Pedestrian starts with the person on foot, adds the facilities made for walkers, and then the dull sense that comes from the slow plod of walking.
sensesIntro.cn: pedestrian 先从「用脚走路的人」出发，加上为步行者建造的设施，最后长出「像走路一样缓慢平淡」的评价义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person who moves on two feet, slow and plain, beside the traffic.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人在车流旁边，用两条腿慢慢走着，普通而缓慢。

branches.en: The person walking is the base sense.
branches.cn: 走路的人是这个基础义项。

branches.en: Facilities for walkers and the older sense of a walking traveller both derive from moving on foot.
branches.cn: 为步行者设的设施，以及「徒步旅人」这一旧义，都源自「用脚走」。

branches.en: Sport once called any competitor on foot a pedestrian.
branches.cn: 旧时体育把任何用脚参赛的人都叫作 pedestrian。

branches.en: Because walking is slow, the word came to criticise dull prose and talk.
branches.cn: 因为走路缓慢，这个词被用来批评平淡的文字与讲话。

branches.en: Unremarkable ideas and the old phrasing of a journey on foot close the range.
branches.cn: 老套的想法与「徒步前往」的旧日说法，收束了全部义项范围。

intro.en: Pedestrian is built from the Latin foot root ped- with the suffix -ian.
intro.cn: pedestrian 由拉丁语「脚」词根 ped- 加上词尾 -ian 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin pes and pedis mean foot, pedestris means going on foot, and pedes is a foot soldier; the same stem gives pedal, pedestal, and expedition.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pes、pedis 意为脚，pedestris 意为步行，pedes 指步兵；同一词干还给出 pedal、pedestal 与 expedition。

items.example: The root ped- comes from Latin pes.
items.exampleCN: 词根 ped- 出自拉丁语 pes。

items.meaning: a person who is or does
items.example: The suffix -ian forms pedestrian from the Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ian 与拉丁词干合成 pedestrian。

items.example: Pedestrian keeps the walking person.
items.exampleCN: pedestrian 保留了「步行的人」。

items.example: Pedestrian as an adjective describes flat style.
items.exampleCN: pedestrian 作形容词时形容平淡的风格。

items.example: The suffix -ise forms pedestrianise.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ise 构成 pedestrianise。

items.meaning: to turn a street into a walking zone
items.example: Pedestrianise names a road change.
items.exampleCN: pedestrianise 指一种道路改造。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms pedestrianised.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 pedestrianised。

items.example: Pedestrianised describes the finished street.
items.exampleCN: pedestrianised 形容改造完成的街道。

items.example: The suffix -ism forms pedestrianism.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ism 构成 pedestrianism。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms pedestrianization.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 pedestrianization。

definition_zh: 儿科医生；儿科医师
definition_en: a doctor who treats babies, children and young people, and who knows how their bodies change as they grow
core_image: 诊室里，一位医生蹲下来，与孩子的视线齐平，轻声说话，再拿起听诊器
scene: 诊室墙上贴着长颈鹿和飞船，走廊里排着抱着婴儿的家长。Anxious parents sat waiting for the pediatrician, holding a feverish baby in their arms.
sceneCN: 这里 pediatrician 是「儿科医生」（第 1 个义项：专门看孩子的医生）；句意：焦急的父母抱着发烧的婴儿，坐着等候儿科医生看病。

collocations.zh: 看儿科医生；咨询儿科医生

collocations.phrase: take the boy to a pediatrician

derivatives.zh: 由词干加表示「学问、学科」的名词尾构成，义为「儿科学」
由词干加表示「属于……的」形容词尾构成，义为「儿科的」
换用另一组「医生」构词成分的同义说法，义为「儿科医生」，较为罕用

senses.title: A doctor of children
senses.definition: a doctor trained to care for babies, children and teenagers, and to judge what is normal at each stage of growth
senses.definitionCN: 受过专门训练、负责照看婴幼儿、儿童与青少年，并判断其各生长阶段是否正常的医生
senses.example: The pediatrician measured the baby and checked her growth chart.
senses.exampleCN: 儿科医生给宝宝量了身高，又查看了成长曲线。
senses.why: Paed-, the child, and iatros, the physician, join into one word whose first duty is the patient who keeps growing.
senses.whyCN: paed- 是「孩子」，iatros 是「医生」，两者合起来，首要职责落在身体不断变化的小病人身上。

senses.title: Clinical partner of the child
senses.definition: a professional who listens to the child as well as to the parent and works alongside nurses, teachers and schools
senses.definitionCN: 既倾听孩子本人、也倾听家长的从业者，并与护士、老师和学校协作
senses.example: The pediatrician asked the boy in private whether the treatment had helped.
senses.exampleCN: 儿科医生私下问那个男孩，治疗有没有效果。
senses.why: Because the patient is young, care has to be arranged for the child as a whole person, inside and outside the clinic.
senses.whyCN: 因为病人年幼，照护必须以孩子这个完整的人为中心来安排，既在门诊之内，也在门诊之外。

senses.title: Clinical use of the specialty
senses.titleCN: 医生与学科的同名用法
senses.definition: in everyday English the same word often names the specialty itself, as when a student says she wants to do pediatrics
senses.definitionCN: 在日常英语里，同一个词也常用来指这门学科本身，比如学生说她想学儿科
senses.example: My cousin is a pediatrician, so the family asks her about every rash.
senses.exampleCN: 我的表姐是儿科医生，所以全家人一有皮疹就问她。
senses.why: The word so strongly points to the trained person that people shorten an appointment to see the pediatrician, folding the doctor and the field into one label.
senses.whyCN: 这个词太明确地指向那位受过训练的人，人们把看诊直接说成去看儿科医生，医生与学科就合用了一个称呼。

intro.en: Pediatrician is built from Greek pais, a child, and iatreia, the art of healing, through a Latin adjective and a French and German name for the field.
intro.cn: 这个词由希腊语 pais（孩子）与 iatreia（医术）构成，经拉丁语形容词、法语与德语里指称该学科的名称，进入英语。

items.en: Pais meant a child and iatros meant a healer; the genitive paιdos supplied the combining stem ped-.
items.cn: pais 指孩子，iatros 指医师；属格 paιdos 给出了构成复合词时使用的词干 ped-。

items.en: Pedia noted the rearing of children, and iatreia the art of curing, which when combined pointed to the healing of children.
items.cn: pedia 表示养育孩子，iatreia 表示医治之术，两者结合便指向对孩子的医治。

items.en: Modern scientific Latin coined pediatria and the adjective pediatricus for the medicine of childhood.
items.cn: 近代科学拉丁语为「童年医学」造出 pediatria 与形容词 pediatricus。

items.en: French pédiatrie and the German term Kinderheilkunde spread the specialty, and English took paediatric with the British spelling.
items.cn: 法语 pédiatrie 与德语中表示「儿童治疗学」的词传播了这门学科，英语随之采用英式拼写 paediatric。

items.en: American English simplified paediatric to pediatric and added the doctor suffix, giving pediatrician; the exact first record of the form is uncertain.
items.cn: 美式英语把 paediatric 简化为 pediatric，再加表示「执业者」的词尾，构成 pediatrician；该拼写首次出现的确切记录不确定。

items.en: Today the word names the doctor, the clinic service and often the whole specialty, while British writing still prefers paediatrician.
items.cn: 今天这个词既指医生，也指门诊服务，还常指整门学科；英式书面语仍偏好 paediatrician。

note.en: The first group shares the Greek child root or the medical ending; the second group gathers the people and services that care for children.
note.cn: 第一组与目标词共享希腊语「孩子」词根或医学后缀；第二组是同样照料孩子的职业与服务。

entries.definition: the branch of medicine that deals with children and their development.
entries.definitionCN: 研究与治疗儿童及其发育的医学分支。

entries.definition: an adjective meaning relating to the medical care of children.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，表示与儿童的医疗照护有关的。

entries.definition: a foot specialist; the spelling looks close, but the root is the Greek word for a foot, so the origins differ.
entries.definitionCN: 足病专科医生；拼写相近，但词根是希腊语中表示「脚」的词，词源不同。

entries.definition: a generic word for a person trained and licensed to treat illness.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指受过训练并获得执照、可以治病的医生的通用说法。

entries.definition: a nurse who is trained to look after children in wards and clinics.
entries.definitionCN: 受过专门训练、在病房和门诊照料孩子的护士。

entries.definition: a doctor who specialises in newborn babies, especially those born early or ill.
entries.definitionCN: 专攻新生儿的医生，尤其擅长照护早产或有病的新生儿。

normalIntro.en: Pediatrician is a transparent compound of the Greek child and healer, with the American spelling favoured in most dictionaries.
normalIntro.cn: pediatrician 是由希腊语「孩子」与「医师」构成的复合词，多数词典以美式拼写作为主条目。

normal.en: The stem ped- means child, as in the adjectives about childcare and children.
normal.cn: 词干 ped- 意为孩子，与「儿童照护」和「儿童」相关的形容词都用它。

normal.en: The ending -iatrician marks a practitioner of medicine.
normal.cn: 词尾 -iatrician 用来标示某科的医学执业者。

normal.en: British spelling keeps the ae, as in paediatrician.
normal.cn: 英式拼写保留 ae，写作 paediatrician。

normal.en: The near twin podiatrist uses a foot root, not a child root.
normal.cn: 形近词 podiatrist 用的是「脚」的词根，而不是「孩子」的词根。

normal.en: Match paed- with education, which marks the rearing of children.
normal.cn: 把 paed- 与 education（教育）联系起来，后者正标记对孩子的养育。

abstract.en: Picture a doctor kneeling so that the eyes are level with a small patient.
abstract.cn: 想象一位医生屈膝跪下，让视线与小病人齐平。

abstract.en: The word is a bridge between the waiting parent and the crying child.
abstract.cn: 这个词像一座桥，一头连着等候的家长，一头连着啼哭的孩子。

abstract.en: Think of a growth chart on the wall: the patient is always changing size.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上那张成长曲线图：这位病人的尺寸永远在变。

examples.en: The pediatrician reassured the mother that the cough was nothing serious.
examples.cn: 儿科医生安慰那位母亲说，这咳嗽并不严重。

examples.en: Families in the village travel two hours to see the only pediatrician at the clinic.
examples.cn: 村里的家庭要坐两小时车，才能见到诊所里唯一的儿科医生。

examples.en: After years in general practice, she trained as a pediatrician in the city hospital.
examples.cn: 做过多年的全科医生之后，她在市医院的儿科接受了专业训练。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮迪亚特瑞申」——像一位医生弯下腰，把「皮」肤和心都贴近小孩；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 pais（孩子，属格 paιdos）给出词干 ped-，iatros（医师）与 iatreia（医术）给出 -iatrician；近代科学拉丁语 pediatria 与法语、德语中表示儿科的名称把这组词带入英语，核心义是「为不断成长的孩子看病的医生」。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as the doctor of growing children, then as the partner of the child in care, and finally as the name people give to the whole specialty.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先指为不断成长的孩子看病的医生，再指照护中孩子那一方的合作者，最后成为人们称呼整门学科的代称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a doctor kneels to meet the child at eye level, stethoscope ready.
core.cn: 核心意象：医生蹲下来与孩子平视说话，听诊器已拿在手边。

branches.en: THE DOCTOR: the trained physician whose patient is a child who keeps changing.
branches.cn: 医生：以不断变化的孩子为病人的受训医师。

branches.en: THE PARTNER: the clinician who listens to the child as well as the parent and works with nurses and schools.
branches.cn: 合作者：既听孩子也听家长，并与护士、学校协作的临床医生。

branches.en: THE SPECIALTY: the everyday name people use for the field and its appointments.
branches.cn: 学科：人们日常用来指这门学科以及看诊的说法。

branches.en: The doctor and the partner are one person seen twice: first as the medical expert, then as the adult friend of the young patient.
branches.cn: 医生与合作者是同一个人的两面：先被看作医学专家，再被看成年幼病人的成年朋友。

branches.en: A single visit brings the doctor and the specialty together, since patients simply call the whole service by the doctor's name.
branches.cn: 一次就诊就把医生与学科连在一起，因为病人干脆用医生的名号来称呼整个服务。

intro.en: Pediatrician is a Greek compound of child and healer, finished with a Latin scientific ending and then an English doctor suffix.
intro.cn: 这个词是希腊语「孩子」与「医师」构成的复合词，加上拉丁语科学词尾，最后再添英语的执业者后缀。

latinIntro.en: Within the word sit Greek pais and iatros, and Latin supplies pediatria, the scientific name for the field.
latinIntro.cn: 词内藏着希腊语 pais 与 iatros，拉丁语则提供了这门学科的科学名称 pediatria。

items.example: The root marks the age of the patient.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根标记病人的年龄。

items.example: British English keeps the ae in paediatrician.
items.exampleCN: 英式英语保留儿科医生一词中的 ae。

items.example: The healer half of the compound comes from here.
items.exampleCN: 复合词中「医师」那一半来自这里。

items.example: It names the medical side of the specialty.
items.exampleCN: 它为这门专业的医学一面命名。

items.example: The Latin coinage fixed the field name.
items.exampleCN: 这一拉丁语新造词固定了学科名称。

items.example: It forms pediatric, the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它构成形容词 pediatric。

items.meaning: a practitioner of a medical field
items.meaningCN: 某一医学领域的执业者
items.example: It forms pediatrician, the doctor.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 pediatrician，即那位医生。

items.example: It forms pediatrics, the field of study.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 pediatrics，即这门学科。

items.meaning: a person who works in a field
items.example: It appears in podiatrist, the foot word.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在表示足病医生的 podiatrist 里。

definition_zh: 血统；谱系；家谱；纯种（动物）；履历；出身
definition_en: the record of the parents and ancestors of a person or animal, and by extension the family line or background that it shows
core_image: 一张展开的树状谱系图，顶端的方框里写着最早的那对父母，线条一层层向下分叉
scene: 拍卖场的围栏里，一匹高大的马站在评委面前，主人把一叠盖着印章的纸张递了过去。The auctioneer praised the stallion as a horse of pure pedigree, bred by a famous stud farm.
sceneCN: 这里 pedigree 是「血统、谱系记录」（第 1 个义项：家畜的血统与谱系）；句意：拍卖师称赞这匹公马血统纯正，出自一家著名的种马场。

pos.zh: 血统；谱系；家谱；纯种（动物）；履历；出身
纯种的；优良血统的；有来头的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加「有……的」形容词尾构成，义为「有血统登记的；纯种的」
由本词加动作名词尾构成，义为「血统的登记与记录」，多见于家畜育种语境
由本词与「分析」构成的复合词组，义为「谱系分析」

senses.title: The recorded bloodline of an animal
senses.titleCN: 家畜的血统与谱系记录
senses.definition: the written record of a horse, dog or other animal's parents and earlier ancestors, kept so that selective breeding is possible
senses.definitionCN: 记录马、狗等动物的父母与历代祖先的书面材料，用于有选择地繁育
senses.example: The kennel club issues a pedigree for every purebred puppy.
senses.exampleCN: 犬业协会会为每一只纯种幼犬开具血统证明。
senses.why: From French pied de grue, a crane's foot, the word first meant a three-branched mark in old family tables, and the table itself was kept for horses and dogs long before human families.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本义是法语「鹤的脚」，指旧式家族表上三叉的标记，而那类表最早被用来记录马和狗的血统。

senses.title: The breeding line behind a person
senses.definition: the line of ancestors from which a person is descended, especially when spoken of as a mark of quality or class
senses.definitionCN: 一个人由之而来的祖先世系，尤其用作身份或等级的标志时
senses.example: Nobody in the village cared about her pedigree; what mattered was her skill with the loom.
senses.exampleCN: 村里没人关心她的家世；重要的是她的织布手艺。
senses.why: The crane-foot branch can be drawn for any family, so the same word moved from the stable to the manor and the family tree.
senses.whyCN: 鹤爪形的分支同样可以为人画出来，于是这个词从马厩走进了庄园与家谱。

senses.title: A traced ancestry of problem cells
senses.definition: a diagram of descent used in genetics and medicine to follow how a trait or a disease passes through blood relatives
senses.definitionCN: 在遗传学与医学中用来追踪某种性状或疾病如何在血亲之间传递的世系图
senses.example: Researchers traced the pedigree to find where the faulty gene had entered the family.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者追踪这份谱系图，找出那个缺陷基因是从哪一代进入这个家族的。
senses.why: Modern genetics needs a map of who came from whom, and the oldest map of that kind was the breeding table, so pedigree became the scientific term for it.
senses.whyCN: 现代遗传学需要一张「谁出自谁」的地图，而最古老的这类地图正是育种表，于是 pedigree 成了它的学术名称。

senses.title: The proven background of a thing
senses.titleCN: 物品、机构或作品的来历与声誉
senses.definition: the history or origin of an object, business, idea or proposal that shows how good it is
senses.definitionCN: 物品、企业、想法或提案的来历与历史，用以说明其品质或可信程度
senses.example: The bank refused the deal because the company had no pedigree in construction.
senses.exampleCN: 银行拒绝了这笔交易，因为这家公司在建筑领域没有可查的资历。
senses.why: If a hound with a known line is trusted, then anything with a known history can be judged the same way, and the word follows the thing it describes.
senses.whyCN: 既然血统可查的猎犬值得信赖，任何有可查来历的东西都能照此评判，这个词便跟着所形容之物走。

senses.title: Purebred as a describing word
senses.titleCN: 形容词：纯种的、有来头的
senses.definition: describing an animal that has recorded pure ancestry, or something that derives its value from an impressive past
senses.definitionCN: 形容继承了纯正且有记录的血统的动物，或形容因显赫来历而显得有价值的事物
senses.example: A pedigree cat in that neighbourhood would be stolen within a week.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个街区，一只纯种猫不到一周就会被人偷走。
senses.why: English uses the noun directly in front of another noun, so the record becomes a quick label of quality.
senses.whyCN: 英语常让名词直接修饰名词，于是这份记录变成一个简洁的质量标签。

intro.en: Pedigree probably comes from Anglo-French pie de grue, a crane's foot, a name the books of old families gave to the three-branched lines that joined parents to children.
intro.cn: pedigree 一般认为来自盎格鲁-法语 pie de grue（鹤的脚），旧式家族谱书的编纂者用这个名字称呼连接父母与子女的三叉线条。

items.en: Pes meant a foot and grus meant a crane or heron, so a crane's foot described three toes spreading from one joint.
items.cn: pes 意为脚，grus 意为鹤或鹭，因此「鹤的脚」就是从一个关节向外张开的三趾。

items.en: Norman scribes in England wrote pie de grue for the spreading lines of a descent table, borrowed from French legal and heraldic usage.
items.cn: 英格兰的诺曼书记官用 pie de grue 来指谱系表中向外分叉的连线，这一用法借自法语的法律与纹章用语。

items.en: English writers turned the phrase into a single word written in several spellings, among them pedigrewe and petigree.
items.cn: 英语写作者把这个词组缩成一个词，出现过 pedigrewe、petigree 等多种拼法。

items.en: Herald and genealogical books used the word for a written line of descent, and the meaning spread to the lineages kept for horses and hounds.
items.cn: 纹章与谱牒书籍用这个词指书面的世系记录，词义随后扩展到记录马与猎犬的血统。

items.en: Farming and the dog and horse show made an animal pedigree a certificate with a market value, and the word became fully commercial.
items.cn: 农业与犬马展会让动物血统变成具有市场价值的证书，这个词也有了充分的商业含义。

items.en: In biology pedigree means a traced line of descent and, in a wider sense, the record of quality behind anything; the precise phonetic history between pie de grue and pedigree remains uncertain.
items.cn: 在生物学中它指追踪出的世系，广义上指任何事物背后的品质来历；从 pie de grue 到 pedigree 之间确切的历史音变过程仍存疑。

note.en: The first group shares the family-tree or descent vocabulary and words that look or sound close; the second group names nearby ideas of line, origin and breeding.
note.cn: 第一组是与谱系、世系相关、或形音相近的词；第二组是与「血脉、出身、繁育」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: an adjective for an animal whose pure ancestry has been officially recorded.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指血统纯正且已获官方记录的动物。

entries.definition: the practice of keeping and checking written breeding records.
entries.definitionCN: 维护并核查书面繁育记录的做法。

entries.definition: a device that counts steps; the opening looks close to the same letters, but the root here is Latin for a foot.
entries.definitionCN: 计步器；开头字母看似相近，但这里的词根是拉丁语的「脚」，词源不同。

entries.definition: a family line, especially of people, traced from one remote ancestor.
entries.definitionCN: 尤指人的家族世系，追溯到某位远祖。

entries.definition: the study of family history and the recording of descent.
entries.definitionCN: 家族史研究与世系记录。

entries.definition: the whole body of a person's ancestors considered as the source of origin.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人的全部祖先，被视为其出身的来源。

normalIntro.en: Pedigree is a picture word: its crane-foot name describes the three-way fork of a family chart, and its modern uses all keep that chart.
normalIntro.cn: pedigree 是一个画面词：鹤脚之名描绘家族表的三角分叉，现代各义项都保留着这张表。

normal.en: The French name pie de grue meant a crane's foot, an image of three toes spreading apart.
normal.cn: 法语 pie de grue 意为「鹤的脚」，是三个脚趾向外张开的形象。

normal.en: A pedigree chart forks exactly like that foot, from one pair down to many offspring.
normal.cn: 谱系图的走向就像那只脚，从一对父母向下一代分叉出去。

normal.en: Horses and dogs first needed written pedigrees, which is why kennel clubs keep the books.
normal.cn: 最早需要书面血统的是马和狗，所以犬业协会一直保留着这些登记册。

normal.en: Lineage and genealogy are its learned neighbours for the human family tree.
normal.cn: lineage 与 genealogy 是它在人类家谱方面的书面邻居。

normal.en: Used before a noun, a pedigree horse and a pedigree company both claim a recorded past.
normal.cn: 放在名词前时，纯种马与有来历的公司都声称自己有一段可查的过去。

abstract.en: A pedigree is less about who you are than about who is written down before you.
abstract.cn: 血统更关心的不是你是何人，而是你之前有谁被登记在册。

abstract.en: Every line on the chart is a choice someone made about which pair to breed.
abstract.cn: 图上的每一条线，都是某个人决定让哪一对相交的选择。

abstract.en: Calling a person pedigreed quietly turns a family into a document of quality.
abstract.cn: 说某人有家世，等于悄悄把一家人变成了一份质量文件。

examples.en: The breeder keeps a pedigree for every litter so that buyers can check the parents.
examples.cn: 繁育者为每一窝幼犬都保留血统记录，方便买家核查其父母。

examples.en: Her pedigree counted for nothing on the factory floor, where speed was all that mattered.
examples.cn: 在车间里，她的家世一文不值，唯一重要的是速度。

examples.en: The clinic used a pedigree built from three generations to trace the disorder.
examples.cn: 诊所利用由三代人构成的谱系图来追踪这种疾病。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拍底格瑞」——拍卖师把一匹马的「血统底细」一张张拍在格里细看；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为来自盎格鲁-法语 pie de grue（鹤的脚），由拉丁语 pes（脚）与 grus（鹤）构成，指谱系表上「三趾般」的分叉线；词形从中古英语 pedigrewe、petigree 演变而来，核心义是「分叉向下、可查的世系线」。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins with the crane-foot chart kept for animals, moves to human families, then to medical descent, and finally to any recorded background and to its adjective use.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先指为动物保存的鹤爪形血统表，再指人的家世，然后进入医学的世系追踪，最后泛指任何可查的来历，并发展出形容词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one pair at the top of the chart sends three branches down to the next generation.
core.cn: 核心意象：图顶的一对父母向下分出三条线，连到下一代。

branches.en: THE STABLE: horses and dogs whose parents are written down for breeding.
branches.cn: 马厩：父母有记录、用于繁育的马与狗。

branches.en: THE FAMILY TREE: the same chart drawn for a person, then asked to trace a disease.
branches.cn: 家谱：同一张图为人画出来，再被用来追踪疾病。

branches.en: THE BACKGROUND: any object, firm or idea whose history vouches for it.
branches.cn: 来历：任何物件、企业或想法的历史为其背书。

branches.en: THE LABEL: the chart used directly to describe something as pure or well-bred.
branches.cn: 标签：这张表被直接用来形容某物纯正、有来头。

branches.en: A breeding record and a business record differ in content, yet both answer the same question: where did this come from.
branches.cn: 血统记录与商业资历内容不同，回答的却是同一个问题：这东西从哪来。

intro.en: Pedigree comes from a French phrase rather than from a Latin prefix: two Latin words for foot and crane sit inside a single English word.
intro.cn: pedigree 并非由拉丁前缀构成，而来自一个法语词组：两个拉丁语词（脚与鹤）藏在同一个英语单词里。

latinIntro.en: Latin pes supplies the foot and grus the crane, while the Anglo-French phrase pie de grue brings them together.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pes 提供「脚」，grus 提供「鹤」，盎格鲁-法语词组 pie de grue 把二者连在一起。

items.example: It is the foot half of the French phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个法语词组里「脚」的那一半。

items.example: It gives the bird whose foot the chart resembles.
items.exampleCN: 它提供谱系图像其脚的那只鸟。

items.example: Scribes used it for a three-branched descent line.
items.exampleCN: 书记官用它来指三叉的世系连线。

items.example: The foot root also appears in words like biped and pedometer.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也出现在 biped 与 pedometer 等词里。

items.structure: French vowel ending kept in the old spelling
items.meaning: the long e at the end of the word
items.meaningCN: 词尾保留法语元音的长 e 音
items.example: Old spellings such as petigree keep an ee ending.
items.exampleCN: petigree 等旧拼写保留 ee 词尾。

items.example: It forms pedigreed, as in a pedigreed hound.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 pedigreed，如 pedigreed hound（有血统记录的猎犬）。

items.example: It forms pedigreeing, the work of recording lines.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 pedigreeing，指记录世系的工作。

items.example: It is not the child root of pediatrician.
items.exampleCN: 它不是 pediatrician 里的「孩子」词根。

items.meaningCN: 孩子（如 pediatric 中所示）
items.example: It explains a look-alike word, not this one.
items.exampleCN: 它能解释形近词，却不能解释本词。

items.example: It builds genealogy, this word's learned neighbour.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 genealogy，也就是本词的书面近邻。

definition_zh: 土壤圈；土壤层
definition_en: the thin outer layer of soil that covers much of the land and where rock, air, water and living things all meet
core_image: 剖面图上，薄薄一层深色土壤贴着地表，下方是岩石，上方是小草和树根，雨水顺着土粒往下渗
scene: 地理课本把地球剖开，标出大气、水、岩石、生物和土壤几层薄壳。The diagram shows how water passes through the pedosphere before it reaches the underground rock.
sceneCN: 这里 pedosphere 是「土壤圈」（第 1 个义项：地表的土壤层）；句意：这张图显示水如何穿过土壤圈，再到达地下岩层。

collocations.phrase: a thin layer of the pedosphere

derivatives.zh: 由本词加表示「属于……的」形容词尾构成，义为「土壤圈的」
与「土壤」词干相关的学科名，义为「土壤学」
同形异义的学科名，指「儿童研究」，与土壤无关

senses.title: The soil shell of the Earth
senses.definition: the part of the earth system made up of soils, considered as one layer between the solid rock below and the living world and air above
senses.definitionCN: 地球系统中由土壤构成的部分，被视为夹在下方基岩与上方生物和空气之间的一层
senses.example: Soil scientists describe the pedosphere as a thin but living skin over the land.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤学家把土壤圈描述为覆盖陆地的一层薄薄而有生命的皮。
senses.why: Pedon is the Greek word for soil and sphaira the word for a ball, so the new scientific compounds give one rounded layer per sphere of the earth.
senses.whyCN: pedon 是希腊语「土壤」，sphaira 是「球」，这类新构的科学复合词为地球的每一圈层都造一个带球字的层名。

senses.title: The meeting place of spheres
senses.definition: the zone where the atmosphere, water, rock and living organisms all interact with soil, which makes it a central place for environmental study
senses.definitionCN: 大气、水、岩石与生物都和土壤相互作用的地带，因此成为环境研究的中心场所
senses.example: Erosion studies focus on the pedosphere because it links rainfall, plant cover and bedrock.
senses.exampleCN: 水土流失研究聚焦于土壤圈，因为它把降雨、植被与基岩联系起来。
senses.why: Soil is not just a substance but a crossing point, because rain, air, roots and broken rock all pass through it, and science needs one name for that junction.
senses.whyCN: 土壤不仅是物质，更是一个交叉点，雨、空气、根系与碎岩都在其中穿行，这种交汇处需要一个统一的名字。

senses.title: The soil archive of the past
senses.definition: the layers and traces held in soil that record past climates, farming and pollution
senses.definitionCN: 土壤中保存的层次与痕迹，记录着过去的气候、耕作与污染
senses.example: Charcoal deep in the pedosphere told the team about ancient burning.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤圈深处的炭屑让研究团队了解到古代的焚烧。
senses.why: Because soil builds up layer by layer and keeps what falls into it, the same layer that supports crops also keeps a written record of earlier ages.
senses.whyCN: 土壤层层堆积，落入其中的东西也被保留，于是托起庄稼的这一层同样为更早的年代留下了书面记录。

intro.en: Pedosphere is a scientific coinage of the twentieth century, joining the Greek word for soil with the Greek word for a sphere and following the naming pattern of atmosphere and biosphere.
intro.cn: pedosphere 是二十世纪的科学新造词，把希腊语「土壤」与希腊语「球」结合起来，沿用 atmosphere 与 biosphere 的命名方式。

items.en: Pedon meant the ground under the foot or the soil itself, and it supplied the soil part of many scientific words.
items.cn: pedon 指脚下的土地或土壤本身，许多科学词里的「土壤」成分都来自它。

items.en: Sphaira meant a ball or globe, and it became the sphere that finishes the names of the earth layers.
items.cn: sphaira 意为球或球体，后来成为层名末尾的 sphere。

items.en: Writers turned sphaira into the English sphere and used it for the rounded shells of the planet, starting with the atmosphere.
items.cn: 学者把 sphaira 变为英语 sphere，用来指地球的圆壳形圈层，最早是 atmosphere。

items.en: Geographers and soil scientists grouped the planet into spheres, and pedosphere joined atmosphere, hydrosphere and biosphere.
items.cn: 地理学家与土壤学家把地球划分为若干圈层，pedosphere 与 atmosphere、hydrosphere、biosphere 并列。

items.en: Russian and then international soil science supported the layer model, so pedosphere became standard in environmental writing.
items.cn: 先是俄罗斯、后是国际土壤学界支持这一圈层模型，pedosphere 遂成为环境写作中的标准词。

items.en: Climate and land management have brought the word into common scientific use, and the exact first printed record of the noun remains uncertain.
items.cn: 气候与土地管理议题让这个词进入常用科学语域，该名词首次见诸印刷的确切记录仍不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the soil root or the sphere ending; the second group names the other earth layers and the study of soil that sits next to it.
note.cn: 第一组与目标词共享「土壤」词根或「球」后缀；第二组是与它并列的其他地球圈层以及相邻的土壤研究。

entries.definition: the scientific study of soils, their formation and classification.
entries.definitionCN: 研究土壤、其形成与分类的科学。

entries.definition: a technical term for a unit of soil examined in profile, from the Greek word for soil.
entries.definitionCN: 从希腊语「土壤」而来的术语，指用于剖面研究的一个土壤单元。

entries.definition: a lever pushed by the foot; it looks close, but its root is the foot, not the soil.
entries.definitionCN: 用脚踩的踏板；拼写相近，但词根是「脚」而非「土壤」，词源不同。

entries.definition: the rigid outer shell of the earth, including the crust and upper mantle.
entries.definitionCN: 地球坚硬的外壳，包括地壳与上地幔。

entries.definition: the zone, from deep soil to high air, in which living things exist.
entries.definitionCN: 生命存在的区域，从土壤深处到高空。

entries.definition: the dark upper layer of soil where most roots and organic matter lie.
entries.definitionCN: 土壤深色的上层，大部分根系与有机质都在这里。

normalIntro.en: Pedosphere imitates atmosphere and biosphere: the green readers of the geosphere keep the -sphere family as a set of earth shells.
normalIntro.cn: pedosphere 摹仿 atmosphere 与 biosphere：熟悉地球科学的读者会把这串 -sphere 当作一组地球圈层。

normal.en: Pedon means soil, so the front of the word names what the sphere is made of.
normal.cn: pedon 意为土壤，所以词的前半告诉你这层球壳由什么构成。

normal.en: Sphaira means a globe, so the -sphere ending always means a rounded layer.
normal.cn: sphaira 意为球，所以 -sphere 词尾永远指一层球壳。

normal.en: Hydrosphere is water, lithosphere is rock, biosphere is life, pedosphere is soil.
normal.cn: hydrosphere 是水，lithosphere 是岩石，biosphere 是生命，pedosphere 是土壤。

normal.en: Pedology is the same root used to name a discipline.
normal.cn: pedology 用同一个词根来为学科命名。

normal.en: Watch the false friend pedal, whose root is the foot rather than the soil.
normal.cn: 注意形近的 pedal，它的词根是脚而不是土壤。

abstract.en: Think of a cake cut open: the thin dark line just under the icing is this layer.
abstract.cn: 想象切开一个蛋糕：糖霜下那一条细细的深色层，就是它。

abstract.en: The soil layer is a skin so thin that concrete alone can seal it.
abstract.cn: 这层土壤薄得像一层皮肤，单独铺一层混凝土就能把它封住。

abstract.en: Rain, air and roots all come through this surface, so scientists call it a meeting place.
abstract.cn: 雨、空气和根系都穿过这个表面，所以科学家称它为交汇地带。

examples.en: The term pedosphere treats all the soils of the world as a single, connected layer.
examples.cn: 「土壤圈」这个术语把世界上所有的土壤视为一个相连的单一圈层。

examples.en: Acid rain damaged the pedosphere around the smelter within a decade.
examples.cn: 冶炼厂周围的土壤圈在十年内就因酸雨受损。

examples.en: Carbon enters the pedosphere through dead roots and leaves and can stay there for centuries.
examples.cn: 碳通过枯根和落叶进入土壤圈，并能在那里留存数百年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「培多斯菲尔」——培育多（培多）的土壤，包住地球一个球（斯菲尔）；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 pedon（土壤、地面）+ 希腊语 sphaira（球），仿照 atmosphere、biosphere 的构词法造出的科学复合词，核心义是「包裹地球并滋养生命的土壤球壳」。

sensesIntro.en: The word names a shell of soil, then the meeting ground of air, water, rock and life, and finally the layer of recorded trace in that soil.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先指一层土壤构成的球壳，再指空气、水、岩石与生命交汇的场所，最后指土壤中留存痕迹的那一层档案。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin dark soil line under the exposed cross-section of the land.
core.cn: 核心意象：地表剖面下一条细细的深色土壤线。

branches.en: THE SHELL: all soils of the land treated as one thin globe-like layer.
branches.cn: 球壳：陆地上的所有土壤被当作一层薄薄的类似球面的层。

branches.en: THE JUNCTION: rain, air, roots and broken rock crossing inside the soil.
branches.cn: 交汇处：雨、空气、根系与碎岩在土壤内部交叉。

branches.en: THE ARCHIVE: traces held in the layers that tell later readers about the past.
branches.cn: 档案：层中留存的痕迹向后来的读者讲述过去。

branches.en: The shell and the junction are the same layer seen from outside and from inside.
branches.cn: 球壳与交汇处是同一层从外面看和从里面看的样子。

branches.en: Because the layer takes in what falls on it, it can hold a diary of what passed.
branches.cn: 因为这一层会接收落在其上的一切，它便能保存一份「过往日记」。

intro.en: Pedosphere is a compound of two Greek words, with soil in front and the layer-forming sphere at the back, in the manner of atmosphere.
intro.cn: pedosphere 是两个希腊语词的复合，前面是土壤，后面是构成层名系列的 sphere，整体仿照 atmosphere 的做法。

latinIntro.en: The word is Greek rather than Latin: pedon supplies soil and sphaira supplies sphere, and both are used today in scientific English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词来自希腊语而非拉丁语：pedon 提供「土壤」，sphaira 提供「球」，两者至今仍用于科学英语。

items.example: The root names the material of the layer.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根点明这一层的构成材料。

items.example: It is the full form behind the short root.
items.exampleCN: 它是简短词根背后的完整形式。

items.example: It forms the names of earth layers.
items.exampleCN: 它构成一连串地球圈层的名称。

items.example: It is the Greek source of the layer ending.
items.exampleCN: 它是这一词尾的希腊语来源。

items.example: It opens atmosphere, the model for this word.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 atmosphere，也就是本词的范本。

items.example: It opens biosphere, the life layer.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 biosphere，即生命圈层。

items.example: It opens hydrosphere, the water layer.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 hydrosphere，即水圈。

items.example: It opens lithosphere, the rock layer.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 lithosphere，即岩石圈。

items.example: It forms pedology, the study of soil.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 pedology，即土壤学。

items.example: It explains pediatric words but not this one.
items.exampleCN: 它能解释与「儿童」有关的词，却不能解释本词。

items.example: It forms pedospheric, the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它构成形容词 pedospheric。

definition_zh: 无与伦比的；无可比拟的；无双的
definition_en: better than everything else of its kind, so that nothing can compare with it
core_image: 一位高手站在比武场上，对面空无一人
scene: 评论家合上节目单，摇头说整台演出没有第二个人能与之相比。The critic closed the programme and said the whole performance was peerless.
sceneCN: 这里 peerless 是「无与伦比的」（第 1 个义项：没有能与之相比的同侪）；句意：评论家合上节目单，摇头说整台演出没有第二个人能与之相比。

pos.zh: 无与伦比的；无可比拟的；无双的

derivatives.zh: 同辈；同等地位的人，是 peerless 的本义来源
由形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「无与伦比」
由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「无与伦比地」

senses.title: Unrivalled in quality
senses.definition: better than all others of the same kind, with no equal
senses.definitionCN: 比同类中的其他一切都好，没有能与之相比的
senses.example: Her peerless command of three languages won her a scholarship.
senses.exampleCN: 她对三门语言无与伦比的掌握为她赢得了奖学金。
senses.why: The suffix -less means without, so peerless describes something that has no peer at all.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -less 表示「没有」，所以 peerless 描述的是完全找不到对手的东西。

senses.title: Without a social equal
senses.titleCN: 没有同等身份者的；无群的
senses.definition: having no person of the same rank, class, or standing nearby
senses.definitionCN: 身边没有同等身份、地位或等级的人
senses.example: In the old village a peerless widow sat apart from the other guests.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个古老的村子里，一位没有同等身份的寡妇坐在其他客人之外。
senses.why: Peer also means a person of the same rank or status, so the adjective can describe someone with no equal around.
senses.whyCN: peer 还表示「同等级、同身份的人」，所以这个词也能形容身边没有同等身份的人。

senses.title: Flawless in execution
senses.definition: done so well that no rival performance could match it
senses.definitionCN: 做得极好，任何对手的表现都无法与之相比
senses.example: The pianist gave a peerless performance that held the hall silent.
senses.exampleCN: 这位钢琴家献上了一场无瑕的演奏，让全场鸦雀无声。
senses.why: When nobody can match a piece of work, the abstract idea of no equal becomes concrete excellence.
senses.whyCN: 当没人能比得上某件作品时，抽象的「无对手」就具体化为「完美」。

senses.title: Beyond comparison
senses.definition: used in formal or literary writing to stress that a thing is beyond comparison
senses.definitionCN: 在正式或文学写作中强调某事物无可比拟
senses.example: The poet praised the peerless beauty of the northern stars.
senses.exampleCN: 诗人赞美了北方星辰无可比拟的美。
senses.why: Because the peerless image has no limit, writers use it for emphasis rather than for factual contrast.
senses.whyCN: 因为「无对手」这一意象没有上限，作家便用它来强调，而不是做事实上的比较。

senses.title: Alone in a class
senses.titleCN: 独领风骚的；同类中唯一的
senses.definition: the single example of its kind, standing alone in its class
senses.definitionCN: 同类中唯一的一个，在自己的类别里孤立无伴
senses.example: The school remained a peerless example of open-air teaching for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校数十年来一直是户外教学独领风骚的范例。
senses.why: The sense of no peer survives even when there is no contest, because the thing has no class to belong to.
senses.whyCN: 即使没有竞争，「没有同侪」的含义依然存在，因为该事物找不到可用于归类的同类。

senses.title: Without historical precedent
senses.definition: without an earlier example that could serve as a match
senses.definitionCN: 没有可供对等比较的先前先例
senses.example: Historians called the reforms peerless in the life of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家称这些改革在这座城市的历程中史无前例。
senses.why: Peer comes from the Latin word for equal, so a thing with no earlier equal is without precedent.
senses.whyCN: peer 源自拉丁语中表示「对等」的词，因此没有先前对等物的事物就是史无前例的。

senses.title: Peerless in art criticism
senses.definition: describing an artist whose skill no contemporary can approach
senses.definitionCN: 描述某位艺术家的技艺同期无人能及
senses.example: Critics called him a peerless colourist of the whole period.
senses.exampleCN: 批评家称他是整个时期卓越超群的色彩大师。
senses.why: The field of art criticism wants absolute praise, so the negative-looking word carries a superlative meaning.
senses.whyCN: 艺术批评需要绝对的赞词，因此这个看似否定的词承载了最高级的含义。

senses.title: Hard to match
senses.titleCN: 难以匹敌的；罕有其匹的
senses.definition: so good in one respect that it is extremely hard for others to match
senses.definitionCN: 在某一方面极出色，别人很难与之匹敌
senses.example: The town is known for its peerless view across the bay.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小镇以望过海湾的难以匹敌的景色闻名。
senses.why: Everyday praise softens the absolute claim into a strong but usable compliment.
senses.whyCN: 日常赞美把绝对的说法弱化为强烈但仍可使用的褒扬。

intro.en: Peerless is peer plus the suffix -less, and peer goes back to Latin par, meaning equal.
intro.cn: peerless 由 peer 加后缀 -less 构成，而 peer 可追溯到拉丁语 par，意为「相等」。

items.en: Par means equal in rank, value, or size.
items.cn: par 意为在等级、价值或大小上相等。

items.en: Per inherits the equal meaning from Latin par.
items.cn: 古法语 per 从拉丁语 par 继承了「相等」的含义。

items.en: Peer names a person of equal rank.
items.cn: 中古英语 peer 指地位相等的人。

items.en: The suffix -less attaches to peer to form peerless.
items.cn: 后缀 -less 与 peer 结合，构成 peerless。

items.en: Peerless spreads into ordinary praise of beauty and skill.
items.cn: peerless 进入日常语境，用于赞美美貌与技艺。

note.en: Peerless belongs to the peer family and sits beside the ordinary words for being better than all others.
note.cn: peerless 属于 peer 一词族，并与表示「胜过一切」的普通词含义相邻。

entries.definition: a person of the same age or rank
the state of having no equal
in a way that has no equal
having no rival
not equalled by anything else
highest in rank or quality

normalIntro.en: Peerless is peer plus less, so the memory hook is a person with no peer around.
normalIntro.cn: peerless 就是 peer 加 less，记忆钩子是「身边没有一个同侪」。

normal.en: Peer means an equal person, so peerless means without an equal.
normal.cn: peer 指地位相等的人，所以 peerless 就是没有相等者。

normal.en: Rival words often keep an n, as in unrivalled, while peerless keeps a silent r sound.
normal.cn: 同类词常保留 n，如 unrivalled，而 peerless 里的 r 音常被省读。

normal.en: Peerless skill appears in reviews and award speeches.
normal.cn: peerless skill 常见于评论与颁奖致辞。

normal.en: The phrase peerless in something says where the quality has no match.
normal.cn: 搭配 peerless in 指出在哪一方面无人能及。

normal.en: Compare unrivalled: both mean no equal, but peerless sounds more literary.
normal.cn: 对比 unrivalled：两者都表示无对手，但 peerless 更具书面色彩。

abstract.en: Picture an empty tournament ring with one champion standing inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一座空荡的比武场，场中只站着一位冠军。

abstract.en: See a ladder with one rung above the top of everyone else.
abstract.cn: 想象一把梯子，在某个人头顶还有一级别人够不到。

abstract.en: Think of a scoreboard whose second place has been erased.
abstract.cn: 想象一块记分牌，第二名的位置被抹掉了。

examples.en: The old bridge is a peerless example of stone building.
examples.cn: 这座古桥是石构建筑无与伦比的范例。

examples.en: She has peerless talent for arranging flowers.
examples.cn: 她在插花方面有无与伦比的才华。

examples.en: Critics agree that the singer is peerless in live performance.
examples.cn: 评论家一致认为这位歌手在现场演出方面无人能及。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮尔勒斯」——皮尔勒斯站在场中央，四周没有一个对手，也就是无与伦比；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 par（相等）→ 古法语 per → 中古英语 peer（同辈）＋ -less（没有）→ peerless，核心义「没有同侪」。

sensesIntro.en: Peerless starts with the absence of an equal person, then widens to superb quality, emphasis, and finally any unmatched thing including history.
sensesIntro.cn: peerless 从「身边没有同等的人」出发，扩展到卓越品质、书面强调，最后泛指任何无可匹敌之物，包括历史先例。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a champion standing alone with no opponent in sight.
core.cn: 核心意象：冠军独自站着，视野里没有对手。

branches.en: No equal becomes outstanding quality.
branches.cn: 没有相等者转变为卓越品质。

branches.en: The social sense keeps the literal peer meaning.
branches.cn: 社会义保留了 peer 的字面含义。

branches.en: Flawless execution is the superlative praise branch.
branches.cn: 完美执行是最高级褒扬的分支。

branches.en: Formal and artistic writing use the word for emphasis.
branches.cn: 正式写作与艺术评论都用它来强调。

branches.en: Alone in a class, without precedent, and hard to match extend the core.
branches.cn: 独一类、无先例、难匹敌三个义项延展了核心。

intro.en: Peerless is peer plus the English suffix -less, with near relatives peer, peerage, and peerless forms.
intro.cn: peerless 由 peer 加英语后缀 -less 构成，近亲有 peer、peerage 以及 peerless 的各种变形。

latinIntro.en: Latin par means equal, and peer entered English through Old French per with that sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 par 意为「相等」，peer 经古法语 per 带着这一含义进入英语。

items.example: Par supplies the equal image.
items.exampleCN: par 提供「相等」的意象。

items.example: Per carries the word into French.
items.exampleCN: per 把这个词带入法语。

items.example: Peer is the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: peer 是整个词族的基础。

items.example: The suffix -less forms peerless.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -less 构成 peerless。

items.example: Peerless names the no-equal image.
items.exampleCN: peerless 命名「无对手」的意象。

items.example: The noun peerlessness means no equal state.
items.exampleCN: 名词 peerlessness 表示没有对手的状态。

items.example: Peerage keeps the rank sense.
items.exampleCN: peerage 保留了「等级」含义。

items.example: The compound uses peer as equal people.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把 peer 用作地位相等的人。

items.example: The phrase shows equal people judging each other.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语显示地位相等者彼此评判。

definition_zh: 待定的；悬而未决的；即将发生的；在……期间
definition_en: waiting to be decided, or about to happen or be released soon
core_image: 一只秤盘挂在梁下，还悬在半空没有落地
scene: 会议开完一半，大家把最后一个议题先放下，等董事会再讨论。The board decided to keep the contract pending until the arrival of the auditor.
sceneCN: 这里 pending 是「待定的」（第 1 个义项：尚未决定、等待裁决）；句意：董事会决定让这份合同的决定悬而未决，直到审计员到来。

pos.zh: 待定的；悬而未决的；即将发生的

derivatives.zh: 由 pendere 加 -ent 构成，义为「悬垂的」
由 pendent 转化而来，义为「悬置状态；待定期间」
im-（向内）＋ pendere（悬挂），义为「即将发生的」
拉丁语 pendulus（悬挂的），义为「钟摆」

senses.title: Waiting to be decided
senses.definition: not yet decided or settled, and waiting for a decision to be made
senses.definitionCN: 尚未决定或确定，等待作出裁决
senses.example: The final decision on the new road is still pending.
senses.exampleCN: 关于这条新路的最终决定仍然悬而未决。
senses.why: The Latin verb pendere means to hang, so something pending hangs undecided like a thing on a hook.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 pendere 意为「悬挂」，所以待定之事就像挂在钩子上，迟迟没有落地。

senses.title: Awaiting a scheduled event
senses.definition: expected to happen soon, so close that it is already in view
senses.definitionCN: 预计很快发生，近得已经在眼前
senses.example: The players looked calm before the pending match.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛即将开始，球员们看上去很平静。
senses.why: A hanging weight swings forward, and the same image becomes something imminent that is already about to fall.
senses.whyCN: 悬挂的重物会向前摆，同一意象就变成「近在眼前、即将落地」的事。

senses.title: Awaiting legal judgment
senses.definition: used of a case, suit, or claim that has been filed and is waiting for a court
senses.definitionCN: 用于已立案正等待法院审理的案件、诉讼或索赔
senses.example: Three lawsuits are pending against the company.
senses.exampleCN: 有三起诉讼正等着对该公司作出审理。
senses.why: Legal language keeps the hanging image: a filed case hangs over the court until judgment.
senses.whyCN: 法律用语保留了「悬挂」意象：立案后案件就悬在法院之上，直到判决。

senses.title: Not yet settled
senses.definition: not yet paid, completed, or finally settled
senses.definitionCN: 尚未支付、完成或最终结清
senses.example: The balance pending on the account must be cleared by Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 账户上未结清的余额必须在周五前清除。
senses.why: Money or work that is pending hangs unfinished, because nobody has brought the account to rest.
senses.whyCN: 未结的钱或工作一直挂着，因为没有谁把它放下来结清。

senses.title: About to be given
senses.definition: ready or about to be released, announced, or printed
senses.definitionCN: 已就绪或即将发布、宣布或刊出
senses.example: The editors held back the pending report until the facts were checked.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑们把即将发表的报告压后，直到事实核查完毕。
senses.why: Publishing sets a deadline, so the hanging thing is only released at publication time.
senses.whyCN: 出版有截稿时间，所以悬而未发的稿子要到刊发那一刻才放下。

senses.title: Overhanging someone
senses.definition: used in formal writing for a threat that stays near and has not yet struck
senses.definitionCN: 正式文体中指尚未发生但始终逼近的威胁
senses.example: A sense of pending danger hung over the whole town.
senses.exampleCN: 一种迫近的危险感笼罩着整座小镇。
senses.why: The core image of hanging returns literally here, because the danger hangs above rather than strikes.
senses.whyCN: 这里重新活用了「悬挂」这一核心意象：危险是悬在上方，而不是已经落下。

senses.title: Waiting on something else
senses.definition: used in the pattern pending something to say that one thing waits on another
senses.definitionCN: 用于 pending something 结构，表示一件事取决于另一件事
senses.example: The funding was released pending the signature of the chair.
senses.exampleCN: 资金在主席签字后方可拨付，是有待签字的。
senses.why: The word turns into a linking phrase that places one event below another in a waiting order.
senses.whyCN: 有的事悬着，是因为要等另一件事先落地，于是这个词就变成了表示等待顺序的连接短语。

senses.title: While waiting
senses.definition: used as a legal or formal preposition to mean while waiting for something
senses.definitionCN: 在正式或法律语境中作介词，表示在等待某事期间
senses.example: The order stands pending a full hearing in court.
senses.exampleCN: 在法院举行完整听证之前，该命令仍然有效。
senses.why: In official documents the word shifts from adjective to preposition, naming the period of hanging.
senses.whyCN: 在正式文件中，这个词从形容词转为介词，直接命名「悬着的那段时间」。

intro.en: Pending is the present participle of the English verb pend, which continues Latin pendere, to hang.
intro.cn: pending 是英语动词 pend 的现在分词，接续拉丁语 pendere，意为「悬挂」。

items.en: Pendere means to hang or to weigh.
items.cn: pendere 意为悬挂或称量。

items.en: The adjective pendens means hanging, still in the air.
items.cn: 形容词 pendens 意为悬挂的、悬而未决的。

items.en: Pendant carries the hanging sense into French.
items.cn: 法语 pendant 延续了「悬垂」的含义。

items.en: The term enters legal English through the Anglo-French phrase.
items.cn: 该词经盎格鲁法语短语进入英国法律英语。

items.en: Pending is used as a preposition meaning during.
items.cn: pending 被用作介词，表示「在……期间」。

items.en: The adjective spreads from courtrooms to offices and news rooms.
items.cn: 形容词用法从法庭扩展到办公室与新闻编辑室。

note.en: Pending belongs to the hanging family and is close to the ordinary words for not yet settled.
note.cn: pending 属于表示「悬挂」的词族，与表示「尚未确定」的普通词含义相近。

entries.definition: a weight hanging and swinging
about to happen
to hang from or rely on
entries.definitionCN: 取决于；依赖（字面为悬挂于）

entries.definition: not yet settled
not yet resolved or paid
waiting for something

normalIntro.en: Pending is the hanging word: something that hangs in the air has not landed yet.
normalIntro.cn: pending 是「悬挂之词」：悬在半空的东西还没落地。

normal.en: The root pend means hang, as in pendant and pendulum.
normal.cn: 词根 pend 表示悬挂，pendant 与 pendulum 都由此而来。

normal.en: Pending payment remains a common phrase on invoices.
normal.cn: pending payment 是发票上的常见说法。

normal.en: In legal writing pending means while waiting for, as in pending trial.
normal.cn: 法律写作中 pending 表示「等待……期间」，如 pending trial 指候审期间。

normal.en: Impending adds im- to the same root and means about to fall on you.
normal.cn: impending 在同一词根前加 im-，表示「即将落到你头上」。

normal.en: Compare pending with undecided: pending is more formal and often legal.
normal.cn: 对比 undecided：pending 更正式，且常用于法律语境。

abstract.en: Picture a suitcase left hanging from a hook, not on the floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一只行李箱挂在钩子上，始终没放到地面。

abstract.en: See a clock hand frozen one minute before the hour.
abstract.cn: 想象钟表的指针停在整点倒数一分钟的位置。

abstract.en: Think of a judge holding a sealed envelope with no date.
abstract.cn: 想象法官拿着一只没写日期的封口信封。

examples.en: The application is still pending while the committee reviews the forms.
examples.cn: 委员会审核表格期间，申请仍在待定中。

examples.en: Two cases against the shop are pending in the local court.
examples.cn: 针对这家店的两起案件正在地方法院待审。

examples.en: The contract was signed pending the final approval of the council.
examples.cn: 合同已签署，有待理事会最终批准。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「碰钉」——事情碰了钉子，就一直悬而未决；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pendere（悬挂、称量）→ pendens（悬着的）→ 英语 pend，再加 -ing → pending，核心义「悬挂未落」。

sensesIntro.en: Pending goes from the hanging state of a decision to an event about to happen, then legal, financial, publishing, threat, and prepositional uses.
sensesIntro.cn: pending 从决定「悬而未落」的状态出发，扩展到即将发生的事，再到法律、财务、出版、威胁以及介词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale pan hanging from a beam, still short of the floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：秤盘挂在横梁下，离地面还差一点。

branches.en: A decision that has not landed is the core sense.
branches.cn: 尚未落地的决定是核心义项。

branches.en: The swing forward becomes an imminent event.
branches.cn: 向前摆动变成即将发生的事件。

branches.en: Court cases keep the hanging image in legal use.
branches.cn: 法庭案件在法律用法中保留了悬挂意象。

branches.en: Money and print jobs hang until settled or released.
branches.cn: 款项与印刷稿件要等到结清或发稿才放下。

branches.en: Threat, dependence, and the while-waiting preposition complete the map.
branches.cn: 威胁、依赖以及「等待期间」的介词用法补全整张图。

intro.en: Pending is pend plus the suffix -ing, and the pend root also builds depend, impend, pendant, and pendulum.
intro.cn: pending 由 pend 加后缀 -ing 构成，pend 词根还构成 depend、impend、pendant 与 pendulum。

latinIntro.en: Latin pendere means to hang or weigh, and pendens means hanging, which fits the pend family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pendere 意为悬挂或称量，pendens 意为悬着的，正好对应 pend 词族。

items.example: Pendere gives the hanging image.
items.exampleCN: pendere 提供悬挂的意象。

items.example: Pendens is the direct Latin ancestor.
items.exampleCN: pendens 是直接的拉丁语祖先。

items.example: Pend is the base verb in English.
items.exampleCN: pend 是英语中的基础动词。

items.meaningCN: 表示进行或状态的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ing forms pending.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 pending。

items.example: Pending stays in the waiting sense.
items.exampleCN: pending 停留在等待含义。

items.example: Pendant keeps the visible hanging.
items.exampleCN: pendant 保留了可见的悬挂。

items.example: Pendulum shows the swinging motion.
items.exampleCN: pendulum 展示摆动。

items.example: Depend adds de- to the root.
items.exampleCN: depend 在词根前加 de-。

items.example: Impending adds im- to the root.
items.exampleCN: impending 在词根前加 im-。

definition_zh: 穿透；渗透；洞察力；市场渗透率
definition_en: the act or process of going into or through something, including into a market or a mind
core_image: 一根针从力的一端扎入，针尖从另一端探出
scene: 医生的细针扎进厚厚的橡胶手套，针尖从另一侧探出一点点。The needle showed little penetration through the thick rubber glove.
sceneCN: 这里 penetration 是「穿透/穿入」（第 1 个义项：进入或穿过有阻力的东西）；句意：这根针几乎没能穿透厚厚的橡胶手套。

pos.zh: 穿透；渗透；洞察力；市场渗透率

derivatives.zh: penetration 去后缀 -ion 的基础动词，义为「穿透；渗入」
penetrate 加 -ing 构成，义为「穿透的；敏锐的」
penetrate 加 -able 构成，义为「可穿透的」
penetrable 加否定前缀 im- 构成，义为「不可穿透的；难以理解的」

senses.title: The act of entering
senses.definition: the act of going into or through something that resists
senses.definitionCN: 进入或穿过的动作
senses.example: The penetration of the needle into the rubber was slow but steady.
senses.exampleCN: 针穿入橡胶的动作缓慢而稳定。
senses.why: The Latin verb penetrare means to put or go inside, so the first sense is simply the force and motion of going in.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 penetrare 意为「放进、深入」，所以第一个义项就是进入的力量与动作。

senses.title: Passing into something
senses.definition: the movement of a substance or force into another body or mass
senses.definitionCN: 物质或力量进入另一个物体或整体的过程
senses.example: The penetration of rain water into the soil fed the roots.
senses.exampleCN: 雨水渗入土壤，滋养了根部。
senses.why: If the verb is put in, then a fluid acts the same way, slowly slipping into the mass.
senses.whyCN: 既然动词是「放进去」，那么流体也以同样方式慢慢渗透进整体内部。

senses.title: Full understanding
senses.definition: the ability to understand a difficult idea or situation deeply
senses.definitionCN: 深入理解困难想法或处境的能力
senses.example: Her penetration into the causes of the crisis impressed the panel.
senses.exampleCN: 她对危机成因的洞察打动了评审团。
senses.why: Mind can penetrate an idea the way a blade penetrates a surface, so a sharp mind goes right through the problem.
senses.whyCN: 心智可以像刀刃穿透表面那样穿透一个想法，所以敏锐的心智能直抵问题核心。

senses.title: Share of a market
senses.titleCN: 市场渗透率；市场占有率
senses.definition: the share of a market that a product or brand has reached
senses.definitionCN: 某一产品或品牌在市场中达到的份额
senses.example: The brand plans to raise penetration in rural areas.
senses.exampleCN: 该品牌计划提高在农村地区的市场渗透率。
senses.why: Business takes the entering image and measures how deeply a product has entered a market.
senses.whyCN: 商业领域借用「进入」意象，衡量产品究竟进入了市场多深。

senses.title: Secret entry
senses.definition: the attempt to get into an enemy or rival organisation without being noticed
senses.definitionCN: 在不被察觉的情况下打入敌方或对手组织
senses.example: The agency reported deep penetration of the smuggling ring.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构报告称已深入渗透走私团伙。
senses.why: When the entering is done in secret, the neutral image of penetration becomes a spy craft.
senses.whyCN: 当「进入」是在暗中进行时，中性的穿透意象就变成了间谍手段。

senses.title: Spread of an idea
senses.definition: the degree to which an idea or custom has spread into a society
senses.definitionCN: 思想或习俗在社会中传播的程度
senses.example: The penetration of printing into daily life changed reading habits.
senses.exampleCN: 印刷术深入日常生活改变了阅读习惯。
senses.why: An idea that goes into a whole society behaves like water in a sponge, so the entering takes on cultural meaning.
senses.whyCN: 思想进入整个社会就像水渗进海绵，于是「进入」获得了文化层面的含义。

senses.title: Depth of physical force
senses.definition: the depth that a weapon, projectile, or beam can reach into a target
senses.definitionCN: 武器、弹丸或光束能侵入目标多深
senses.example: Engineers tested the penetration of the new armour plate.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师们测试了新装甲板的穿透深度。
senses.why: Physical science needs a measure, so the entering image becomes a depth number on a test chart.
senses.whyCN: 物理科学需要一个量度，于是「进入」的意象变成了测试图表上的深度数值。

senses.title: Sexual sense
senses.definition: a formal or clinical term for the entry of the penis into the body
senses.definitionCN: 医学或书面语境中指阴茎进入身体的正式用语
senses.example: The health guide describes penetration without using slang terms.
senses.exampleCN: 这本健康指南不用俚语，而是描述插入行为。
senses.why: The same entering meaning is used clinically, because the neutral verb suits medical writing.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「进入」含义被用于临床，因为中性动词适合医学写作。

senses.title: Insight on a topic
senses.definition: the quality of a remark or of an analysis that reaches the heart of a matter
senses.definitionCN: 评论或分析直抵要害的品质
senses.example: His essay shows unusual penetration for such a young writer.
senses.exampleCN: 对于如此年轻的作者，他的文章显出不同寻常的深刻。
senses.why: A remark that enters the heart of a matter is praised as penetrating, so the noun names that quality.
senses.whyCN: 能进入问题核心的言论被赞为「透彻」，于是名词本身就指这种品质。

intro.en: Penetration comes from Latin penetrare, to put or go inside, with the noun penetratio behind the English form.
intro.cn: penetration 来自拉丁语 penetrare，意为「放进、深入」，其名词 penetratio 构成英语形式。

items.en: Penetrare means to put in or enter deeply.
items.cn: penetrare 意为放入或深入。

items.en: Penetratio names the act of entering.
items.cn: penetratio 指进入的行为。

items.en: The noun enters medical writing first.
items.cn: 这个名词最早进入医学写作。

items.en: The word extends to mental and figurative entry.
items.cn: 该词扩展到心智与比喻意义上的深入。

items.en: Business and computer security add market and network uses.
items.cn: 商业与安全领域增加了市场与网络用语。

note.en: Penetration belongs to the Latin penetro family and is close to the ordinary words for going through.
note.cn: penetration 属于拉丁语 penetro 词族，与表示「穿过」的普通词含义相近。

able to be entered
secret entry into an organisation
spreading through every part

normalIntro.en: Penetration is the noun of going in: the needle, the idea, the product all pierce a surface.
normalIntro.cn: penetration 是「进入」的名词：针、思想、产品都在刺穿一层表面。

normal.en: Penetrate is the verb, and -ion turns its action into a noun.
normal.cn: penetrate 是动词，-ion 把动作变成名词。

normal.en: Im- in impenetrable means not, so it describes a surface that stops the entry.
normal.cn: impenetrable 中的 im- 表示「不」，描述挡住进入的表面。

normal.en: Market penetration counts how deep a product has reached.
normal.cn: market penetration 计算产品渗透得有多深。

normal.en: Penetration test is a standard term in computer security.
normal.cn: penetration test 是计算机安全领域的标准说法。

normal.en: Compare infiltration: it is secret and mainly military, while penetration can be physical and neutral.
normal.cn: 对比 infiltration：后者偏军事与秘密，而 penetration 可以是物理且中性的。

abstract.en: See a pin pushing slowly through a thick sponge.
abstract.cn: 想象一根大头针慢慢穿透厚海绵。

abstract.en: Picture sunlight going through thin leaves in several places.
abstract.cn: 想象阳光从好几个地方透过薄叶。

abstract.en: Think of a key slipping into a lock with a click.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙咔哒一声滑进锁孔。

examples.en: The company reported strong market penetration in Asia.
examples.cn: 公司报告称在亚洲取得了很强的市场渗透。

examples.en: The penetration of the knife was stopped by the leather.
examples.cn: 刀子被皮革挡住了，没能穿透。

examples.en: Her penetration into the motives of the mayor surprised the reporters.
examples.cn: 她对市长动机的洞察让记者们惊讶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮内穿」——针穿过皮内，就是穿透；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 penitus（深处、内部）→ penetrare（深入、穿透）→ penetratio → 法语 pénétration → 英语 penetration，核心义「深入内部」。

sensesIntro.en: Penetration begins with the physical act of going in, then spreads to substances, understanding, markets, secrecy, ideas, force, the body, and sharp comments.
sensesIntro.cn: penetration 从物理上的「进入」开始，再扩展到物质渗入、理解、市场、秘密行动、思想传播、力量、身体以及评论深度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle pushing into a thick surface and showing at the other side.
core.cn: 核心意象：针扎进厚表面，从另一侧探出。

branches.en: The physical act of entry is the core.
branches.cn: 物理上的进入动作是核心。

branches.en: Substances pass into other bodies.
branches.cn: 物质进入其他物体内部。

branches.en: The sharp mind reaches the heart of a matter.
branches.cn: 敏锐的心智直抵问题要害。

branches.en: Markets, secrets, and ideas are entered as well.
branches.cn: 市场、秘密与思想同样被「进入」。

branches.en: Force and body give measured and clinical entries.
branches.cn: 力量与身体造成可量化的、临床的进入。

intro.en: Penetration is penetrate plus the suffix -ion, built on the Latin penetro family.
intro.cn: penetration 由 penetrate 加后缀 -ion 构成，源自拉丁语 penetro 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin penetrare means to enter deeply, and penitus means deep inside.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 penetrare 意为深入，penitus 意为深在内部。

items.example: Penitus gives the deep image.
items.exampleCN: penitus 提供「深处」的意象。

items.example: Penetrare is the direct verb ancestor.
items.exampleCN: penetrare 是直接的动词祖先。

items.example: Penetratio is the Latin noun source.
items.exampleCN: penetratio 是拉丁语名词来源。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或过程的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ion forms penetration.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ion 构成 penetration。

items.example: Penetrate is the base verb.
items.exampleCN: penetrate 是基础动词。

items.example: Penetration keeps the entering noun.
items.exampleCN: penetration 保留「进入」的名词义。

items.example: Penetrating describes a sharp mind.
items.exampleCN: penetrating 描述敏锐的头脑。

items.example: The prefix im- forms impenetrable.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 im- 构成 impenetrable。

items.example: The suffix -able forms penetrable.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 构成 penetrable。

items.example: Impenetrable negates the ability.
items.exampleCN: impenetrable 对能力加以否定。
